paras.zh: 美国贸易代表办公室特别指出韩国专注于存储芯片生产，并称其政府支持力度过大。然而，它将该国的芯片排除在拟议的产能过剩关税之外。

paras.en: Taiwan, which faces an excess-capacity tariff cap of 15%, also benefits from exemptions for other electronics, including mobile phones and networking equipment. Its effective tariff rate would rise to about 9% from 6%, Williams estimated.
paras.zh: 台湾面临15%的过剩产能关税上限，也受益于其他电子产品的豁免，包括手机和网络设备。威廉姆斯估计，其有效关税将从 6% 升至 9% 左右。

paras.en: — CNBC's Evelyn Cheng contributed to this report.
paras.zh: — CNBC 的 Evelyn Cheng 对本报告作出了贡献。

articles.title: Norse Atlantic suspends all flights, warns it may file for bankruptcy after share price collapse

paras.en: Norse Atlantic suspended all of its flights on Thursday and warned it may have to file for bankruptcy after its stock collapsed on Wednesday following its warning about its "critical" financial situation.
paras.zh: 挪威大西洋航空公司周四暂停了所有航班，并警告称，在其对其“危急”财务状况发出警告后，周三股价暴跌，该公司可能不得不申请破产。

paras.en: Oslo-listed shares of Norse closed 85% lower on Wednesday.
paras.zh: Norse 在奥斯陆上市的股票周三收盘下跌 85%。

paras.en: "The board of directors continues to consider options to secure short-term financing," Norse said in a Thursday statement. "If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the board's intention to file for bankruptcy."
paras.zh: 诺斯在周四的声明中表示：“董事会继续考虑确保短期融资的选择。” “如果不能紧急找到短期融资解决方案，董事会打算申请破产。”

paras.en: The airline added that "there can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found."
paras.zh: 该航空公司补充说，“不能保证会找到可行的解决方案。”

paras.en: Checks by CNBC showed the airline was still selling tickets for flights on Friday and beyond as of 9 a.m. Oslo time on Thursday.
paras.zh: CNBC 的检查显示，截至奥斯陆时间周四上午 9 点，该航空公司仍在销售周五及以后航班的机票。

paras.en: Warning signs first popped up when PK786 from London to Islamabad and PK710 from Manchester to Lahore were cancelled because of "an unexpected operational suspension," the Pakistani flag carrier said on X.
paras.zh: 巴基斯坦国旗航空公司 X 表示，由于“意外的运营暂停”，从伦敦飞往伊斯兰堡的 PK786 航班和从曼彻斯特飞往拉合尔的 PK710 航班被取消，警告信号首次出现。

paras.en: The airline had been set to operate two Pakistan International Airlines flights Wednesday under a wet-lease agreement, in which one airline provides the aircraft and crew to another. The agreement had only been signed in early October.
paras.zh: 该航空公司原定于周三根据湿租赁协议运营巴基斯坦国际航空的两架航班，其中一家航空公司向另一家航空公司提供飞机和机组人员。该协议于10月初才签署。

paras.en: PIA said it would operate the routes using its own Boeing 777 aircraft from Wednesday.
paras.zh: 巴基斯坦国际航空表示，将从周三开始使用自己的波音 777 飞机运营这些航线。

paras.en: Norse's own flight Z0 783 from London Gatwick to Orlando was also shown as canceled Wednesday on live air traffic website Flightradar24. London Gatwick's website listed the flight's status for Thursday as "enquire airline."
paras.zh: Norse 自己的从伦敦盖特威克机场飞往奥兰多的 Z0 783 航班周三在实时空中交通网站 Flightradar24 上也显示被取消。伦敦盖特威克机场的网站将周四该航班的状态列为“查询航空公司”。

paras.en: In a bid to stave off financial troubles, Norse cut 75 jobs in May as part of an effort to reduce costs by $50 million, after Eivind Roald replaced founder Bjorn Tore Larsen as CEO in November last year.
paras.zh: 去年 11 月 Eivind Roald 取代创始人 Bjorn Tore Larsen 担任首席执行官后，为了避免财务困境，Norse 在 5 月份裁员 75 人，以削减 5000 万美元的成本。

paras.en: The Norwegian carrier said Wednesday that its situation depended on securing financing for short-term liquidity needs and that it was in discussions about a potential strategic takeover.
paras.zh: 这家挪威航空公司周三表示，其情况取决于能否获得满足短期流动性需求的融资，并且正在讨论潜在的战略收购。

paras.en: "Norse is also engaged in discussions with selected parties on short term financing, however, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution," the airline said.
paras.zh: 该航空公司表示：“挪威航空公司还在与选定的各方就短期融资进行讨论，但不能保证此类讨论会产生可行的解决方案。”

paras.en: India's largest airline, low-cost carrier IndiGo, entered an agreement with Norse Atlantic in early 2025 to lease six 787-9 aircraft as it launched flights to Europe and Britain ahead of the arrival of its own widebody planes.
paras.zh: 印度最大的航空公司、低成本航空公司靛蓝航空 (IndiGo) 于 2025 年初与挪威大西洋航空公司 (Norse Atlantic) 达成协议，租赁六架 787-9 飞机，以在其自己的宽体飞机抵达之前开通飞往欧洲和英国的航班。

paras.en: The agreement concluded at the end of October this year, with IndiGo citing airspace constraints, elevated fuel costs and currency pressures.
paras.zh: 该协议于今年 10 月底签订，靛蓝航空的理由是空域限制、燃料成本上升和货币压力。

paras.en: At its peak in 2024, Norse Atlantic had 4,822 scheduled flights. That number dipped to 4,695 in 2025 and 2,565 in 2026, according to aviation analyst Cirium. The airline had 122 flights scheduled for November this year.
paras.zh: 在 2024 年的高峰期，挪威大西洋航空公司有 4,822 趟定期航班。据航空分析师 Cirium 称，这一数字到 2025 年将降至 4,695 架，到 2026 年将降至 2,565 架。该航空公司今年 11 月计划有 122 个航班。

paras.en: Norse Atlantic CEO Roald told CNBC in May that he was not "overly concerned" about access to fuel and said the airline had no indication at the time that the crisis would have an immediate impact. The airline said in October that it was continuing to operate at reduced capacity because of "prolonged high fuel prices."
paras.zh: 挪威大西洋航空公司首席执行官罗尔德今年 5 月向 CNBC 表示，他并不“过度担心”燃料供应问题，并表示该航空公司当时没有迹象表明这场危机会产生立竿见影的影响。该航空公司十月份表示，由于“燃油价格长期居高不下”，它将继续以减少运力的方式运营。

paras.en: Correction: This story was updated to reflect that Norse shares closed 85% lower on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 更正：本文已更新，以反映 Norse 股价周三收盘下跌 85%。

articles.title: Global stocks rally as investors shrug off U.S. tariffs and AI jitters

paras.en: Global stocks rallied on Thursday, staging a tentative recovery from an intense AI-driven sell-off and looked past a fresh set of tariffs unveiled by the White House on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 全球股市周四上涨，从人工智能驱动的剧烈抛售中暂时复苏，并超越了白宫周三公布的一系列新关税。

paras.en: U.S. markets will be closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday and will have a shortened trading session on Friday. During Wednesday's regular session, the Dow gained 0.33%, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% and the S&P 500 shed 0.25%.
paras.zh: 美国市场周四因感恩节假期休市，周五交易时段缩短。在周三的常规交易中，道指上涨 0.33%，以科技股为主的纳斯达克综合指数下跌 0.62%，标准普尔 500 指数下跌 0.25%。

paras.en: In Europe on Thursday, equities rose sharply. The pan-European Stoxx 600 was 1.4% higher shortly after the opening bell, with all sectors and major bourses in positive territory.
paras.zh: 周四欧洲股市大幅上涨。开盘后不久，泛欧斯托克 600 指数上涨 1.4%，所有板块和主要交易所均上涨。

paras.en: Germany's DAX led gains on a rise of 1.7%, while the Stoxx 600 Technology index jumped almost 2%. The regional tech index has lost more than 12% so far this month, amid jitters around a potential AI bubble bursting and the ousting — and return — of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO.
paras.zh: 德国 DAX 指数上涨 1.7%，斯托克 600 科技指数上涨近 2%。由于人工智能泡沫可能破裂以及黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 被罢黜并重新担任 Nvidia 首席执行官，本月迄今为止，该地区科技指数已下跌超过 12%。

paras.en: German semiconductor firm Infineon was more than 4% higher in early trading, as chip stocks notched a boost. ASMI and ASML gained 2.8% and 2.4%, respectively, while Be Semiconductor added close to 3%.
paras.zh: 由于芯片股上涨，德国半导体公司英飞凌早盘股价上涨逾 4%。 ASMI 和 ASML 分别上涨 2.8% 和 2.4%，Be Semiconductor 上涨近 3%。

paras.en: Asia-Pacific markets also rose on Thursday.
paras.zh: 周四亚太股市也上涨。

paras.en: South Korea's Kospi gained 0.29% to close at 4,711.21, while the small-cap Kosdaq index advanced 0.78% to 655.71 after the country's central bank hiked benchmark lending rates to a 2-year high, in its final meeting of the year.
paras.zh: 韩国央行在今年最后一次会议上将基准贷款利率上调至两年高点，韩国综合股价指数上涨 0.29%，收于 4,711.21 点，而小型股科斯达克指数上涨 0.78%，至 655.71 点。

paras.en: Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.86% to 57,499.16 while the Topix edged 0.11% higher to 3,750.4. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.82% to 8,763.8.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was up 1.52% in its last hour of trade, while mainland China's CSI 300 edged higher marginally, closing at 3,900.55.
paras.zh: 香港恒生指数最后一小时上涨1.52%，而中国内地沪深300指数小幅走高，收于3,900.55点。

paras.en: Asian technology stocks rebounded sharply Thursday, led by Japanese chip-related companies.
paras.zh: 亚洲科技股周四大幅反弹，其中日本芯片相关公司领涨。

paras.en: SoftBank Group surged more than 7%, while chip-testing equipment maker Advantest rose 4.57%. Lasertec and Disco gained , while Tokyo Electron climbed 0.59%
paras.zh: 软银集团股价飙升逾 7%，芯片测试设备制造商 Advantest 股价上涨 4.57%。 Lasertec 和 Disco 上涨，而 Tokyo Electron 上涨 0.59%

paras.en: In South Korea, memory chip giants SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics advanced more than 2% and 0.35%, respectively. The gains followed a bruising session Wednesday amid renewed concerns over the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending.
paras.zh: 在韩国，存储芯片巨头SK海力士和三星电子分别上涨超过2%和0.35%。由于人们再次担心人工智能支出的可持续性，周三股市出现了惨重的上涨。

paras.en: Cryptocurrencies also traded higher, with bitcoin rising 1.58% to $60,944.60, while ether gained 1.15% to $1,702.96.
paras.zh: 加密货币也走高，比特币上涨 1.58% 至 60,944.60 美元，而以太币上涨 1.15% 至 1,702.96 美元。

paras.en: The gains come amid lingering concerns over the outlook for digital assets, with the co-founder of now-shuttered crypto exchange BitMEX Arthur Hayes telling CNBC on Tuesday that bitcoin could test $50,000 if the Nasdaq continues to slide.
paras.zh: 比特币上涨之际，人们对数字资产前景的担忧挥之不去，现已关闭的加密货币交易所 BitMEX 联合创始人 Arthur Hayes 周二向 CNBC 表示，如果纳斯达克继续下滑，比特币可能会测试 50,000 美元。

paras.en: Meanwhile, fresh U.S. inflation data reinforced expectations of further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve. The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.8% year on year in October, accelerating from 3.7% in September, while core inflation came in slightly above expectations at 3.3%.
paras.zh: 与此同时，美国最新通胀数据强化了美联储进一步收紧货币政策的预期。 10 月份个人消费支出价格指数同比上涨 3.8%，较 9 月份的 3.7%有所加快，而核心通胀率略高于预期，为 3.3%。

articles.title: This is the best time to eat Thanksgiving dinner for your health

paras.en: The holiday season is here, and many of us are planning elaborate feasts to celebrate. Whether they’re Thanksgiving turkey dinners or Hanukkah latkes or Christmas roasts, these meals often stretch for hours at time. As you plan your menu, the timing of it all becomes paramount—including when you will sit down to eat. But does eating at, say, 3 P.M. rather than 7 P.M. make a real difference?
paras.zh: 假期到了，我们许多人都在计划精心准备的盛宴来庆祝。无论是感恩节火鸡大餐、光明节马铃薯饼还是圣诞烤肉，这些餐点通常会持续几个小时。当你计划菜单时，时间安排就变得至关重要——包括你什么时候坐下来吃饭。但是，比如说，下午 3 点吃饭吗？而不是晚上 7 点真正发挥作用吗？

paras.en: The answer is yes—and it influences your health more than you think.
paras.zh: 答案是肯定的，而且它对您健康的影响比您想象的还要大。

paras.en: An entire area of science called chrononutrition is dedicated to how when we eat affects our bodies. Essentially, it is the study of how the timing, frequency and regularity of meals interact with the body’s internal biological clock to influence health.
paras.zh: 称为“计时营养”的整个科学领域致力于研究我们的饮食如何影响我们的身体。本质上，它是研究进餐的时间、频率和规律如何与人体内部生物钟相互作用以影响健康。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “People who consume the same number of calories throughout the day but at different times can experience different responses—for example, in terms of weight loss and blood glucose levels,” says Gabriela Pereira, a researcher in chrononutrition at the Federal University of Uberlândia in Brazil.
paras.zh: 巴西乌贝兰迪亚联邦大学的计时营养学研究员加布里埃拉·佩雷拉 (Gabriela Pereira) 表示：“全天但在不同时间摄入相同热量的人可能会经历不同的反应，例如体重减轻和血糖水平。”

paras.en: Dietary advice traditionally focuses on food quality, calories, macronutrients and portion sizes. But when we eat matters perhaps just as much as these other factors, Pereira says.
paras.zh: 饮食建议传统上侧重于食品质量、卡路里、常量营养素和份量。但佩雷拉说，我们什么时候吃东西可能和其他因素一样重要。

paras.en: Our bodies do not process food in the same way throughout the day. Metabolism, insulin sensitivity and hormonal activity fluctuate according to our internal circadian clock. And these rhythms are themselves individual and described by a characteristic known as chronotype.
paras.zh: 我们的身体一天中处理食物的方式并不相同。新陈代谢、胰岛素敏感性和激素活性根据我们的内部生物钟而波动。这些节律本身是个体的，并由一种称为“计时型”的特征来描述。

paras.en: Most people generally fall into two broad categories: “larks,” or morning types, who naturally wake up early, have more energy in the morning and tend to eat earlier in the day, and “night owls,” or evening types, who prefer staying up late and waking up later and tend to eat most in the afternoon and evening. Which bucket you fall into may be related to levels of hormones that help regulate activity and rest, such as cortisol and melatonin.
paras.zh: 大多数人通常分为两大类：“百灵鸟”或早起型，他们自然起得很早，早上精力充沛，往往在一天中吃得较早；“夜猫子”或“夜猫子”，他们喜欢熬夜，晚起，往往在下午和晚上吃得最多。您属于哪一类可能与有助于调节活动和休息的激素水平有关，例如皮质醇和褪黑激素。

paras.en: In night owls, for example, hormone release may be more “delayed” than in larks, Pereira explains. As a result, hunger signals may also ping later, meaning that these individuals may not feel the need to eat immediately after waking up and may skip breakfast. But regardless of your chronotype, there is evidence that eating large meals earlier in the day may be more beneficial for your health.
paras.zh: 例如，佩雷拉解释说，夜猫子的激素释放可能比百灵鸟更“延迟”。因此，饥饿信号也可能会稍后发出，这意味着这些人在醒来后可能不会立即感到需要吃东西，并且可能会不吃早餐。但无论您的生物钟类型如何，有证据表明，在一天中早些时候吃大餐可能对您的健康更有益。

paras.en: “Having a festive meal in the early afternoon is the ideal choice from a biological standpoint because it is a time when the body is better able to handle carbohydrates, fats and large portions,” explains Giovanna Muscogiuri, a professor of medicine at the University of Arizona.
paras.zh: 亚利桑那大学医学教授乔凡娜·穆斯科吉里 (Giovanna Muscogiuri) 解释说：“从生物学角度来看，在午后吃一顿节日大餐是理想的选择，因为此时身体能够更好地处理碳水化合物、脂肪和大量食物。”

paras.en: Insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance are typically high in the morning and decline as the day progresses. This means that consuming a lot of carbohydrates and sugars late at night could spike blood glucose more than eating the same meal at lunchtime.
paras.zh: 胰岛素敏感性和葡萄糖耐量通常在早晨较高，并随着时间的推移而下降。这意味着深夜摄入大量碳水化合物和糖可能比午餐时吃同样的饭菜使血糖升高更多。

paras.en: Even on holidays, Muscogiuri says, try not to skip breakfast—instead have a small, protein-rich meal. This helps the body take advantage of the morning cortisol peak and may prevent energy dips that could lead to overeating later in the day. If you do choose to hold an evening celebration, try to finish eating at least three hours before going to bed.
paras.zh: 马斯科吉里说，即使在假期，也尽量不要不吃早餐，而是吃一顿富含蛋白质的小餐。这有助于身体利用早晨皮质醇的峰值，并可能防止能量下降，从而导致当天晚些时候暴饮暴食。如果您确实选择举办晚间庆祝活动，请尝试在睡觉前至少三个小时吃完饭。

paras.en: What you eat when during the meal also matters, Muscogiuri says. Start with fiber-rich vegetables, followed by protein and fats. Complex carbohydrates and desserts can be saved for the end.
paras.zh: Muscogiuri 说，吃饭时吃什么也很重要。从富含纤维的蔬菜开始，然后是蛋白质和脂肪。复杂的碳水化合物和甜点可以留到最后。

paras.en: “By eating them last, carbohydrates enter an intestinal environment where absorption has already been slowed by fiber and fats, thereby helping to prevent a so-called blood sugar spike,” Muscogiuri says.
paras.zh: “通过最后吃碳水化合物，碳水化合物进入肠道环境，其中的吸收已经被纤维和脂肪减慢，从而有助于防止所谓的血糖峰值，”Muscogiuri 说。

paras.en: Both Pereira and Muscogiuri emphasize, however, that we do not need to worry too much about the metabolic effects of a single meal. Celebrations such as Thanksgiving are special occasions, after all. “It is habitual behavior, rather than an occasional exception, that can have harmful effects,” Muscogiuri says.
paras.zh: 然而，佩雷拉和穆斯科吉里都强调，我们不需要过多担心单餐的代谢影响。毕竟，感恩节等庆祝活动是特殊的场合。 “可能产生有害影响的是习惯性行为，而不是偶尔的例外，”Muscogiuri 说。

articles.title: A new biography reveals the private life of Stephen Hawking

paras.en: Rachel Feltman: For Scientific American’s Science Quickly, I’m Rachel Feltman.
paras.zh: 雷切尔·费尔特曼：《科学美国人》的《科学快报》，我是雷切尔·费尔特曼。

paras.en: If I asked you to name the most famous scientists of the 20th century—or even of all time—I bet Stephen Hawking would end up somewhere on your list. But how much do you really know about this iconic physicist?
paras.zh: 如果我让你说出 20 世纪甚至有史以来最著名的科学家的名字，我敢打赌斯蒂芬·霍金最终会出现在你的名单上。但您对这位标志性物理学家真正了解多少？

paras.en: In his new book Hawking: His Life and Work, award-winning science writer and biographer Graham Farmelo draws on years of research to explore Hawking’s complicated personal story. Scientific American’s books and culture lead Bri Kane recently sat down with Graham to chat. Here’s their conversation.
paras.zh: 屡获殊荣的科学作家兼传记作家格雷厄姆·法梅洛在他的新书《霍金：他的生活与工作》中，利用多年的研究来探索霍金复杂的个人故事。 《科学美国人》的图书和文化负责人布里·凯恩最近与格雷厄姆坐下来聊天。这是他们的对话。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Bri Kane: The sources on this is really incredible. I mean, the level of detail of knowing what he had for breakfast some days, and what his mother went home and, and wrote in her journal about him that day. It’s pretty extraordinary. What was he like as a child? Because the first few hundred pages of this book, he’s a child. Like, he’s under 18. He’s in school. He’s playing with his friends. And I’d never really heard about that part of his life before. So I wanted to ask you about your research and your sources into his childhood.
paras.zh: Bri Kane：这方面的消息来源确实令人难以置信。我的意思是，了解他某天早餐吃了什么，以及他母亲那天回家后在日记中写下的关于他的细节。这非常了不起。他小时候是什么样的？因为这本书的前几百页，他还是个孩子。比如，他还不到 18 岁。他在上学。他正在和他的朋友们一起玩。我以前从未真正听说过他生活的这一部分。所以我想问一下你对他童年的研究和资料来源。

paras.en: Graham Farmelo: Two things. First of all, the very early life of Stephen Hawking, that is illuminated in my book thanks to the wonderful work of his father in keeping a journal for 60 years, right, which started in the 1920s. One of the things he longed for was a son; he wrote diligently, sometimes almost every day, about Stephen Hawking. That and the writings of his mother give an extraordinarily rich feel for the growth of Stephen Hawking and, I would say, help illuminate why Hawking became the person he is.
paras.zh: 格雷厄姆·法梅洛：有两件事。首先，史蒂芬·霍金的早年生活，这在我的书中得到了阐述，这要归功于他父亲从 1920 年代开始的 60 年记日记的出色工作，对吧。他渴望的事情之一就是有个儿子；他勤奋地写关于史蒂芬·霍金的文章，有时几乎每天都写。这些以及他母亲的著作给史蒂芬·霍金的成长带来了异常丰富的感觉，我想说，这有助于阐明霍金为何成为现在的样子。

paras.en: Well, his school days, I can’t tell you the good fortune I had there because I managed to meet with, I think it was about half a dozen of his school chums, and I actually became very good friends with his best friend at school, John McClenahan. Lovely man. I think he was very lucky to meet Stephen. I was very lucky to meet John. John died last Christmas Eve, and I was the last person to have lunch with him, right? And John read, reread, checked and facilitated a lot of the detail, right, of that amazing duo that was Hawking and McClenahan because they were seen as the kind of Lennon-McCartney of the Meccano model, and Stephen was the person that came out with the big dramatic ideas like. But John was the person who made it happen, and you needed them both, you know.
paras.zh: 好吧，在他的学生时代，我无法告诉你我在那里有多么幸运，因为我设法见到了他的六位同学，实际上我和他在学校最好的朋友约翰·麦克莱纳汉成了很好的朋友。可爱的男人。我认为他很幸运能够见到斯蒂芬。我很幸运能够见到约翰。约翰去年平安夜去世了，我是最后一个和他共进午餐的人，对吧？约翰读了、重读、检查并促进了霍金和麦克莱纳汉这个令人惊叹的二人组的许多细节，因为他们被视为麦卡诺模型中的列侬-麦卡特尼，而斯蒂芬是提出诸如此类的重大戏剧性想法的人。但约翰是让这一切发生的人，你知道，你需要他们两个。

paras.en: So again, all I read before was that John and Stephen worked together. But with him, he was sending me dozens of e-mails of picturing the devices they made. So anyway, it was a real experience to get to know. And I’m sad to say some of those people have died since that research has been done. So future Hawking biographers are not going to have, I’m sad to say, access to those people.
paras.zh: 再说一次，我之前读到的都是约翰和斯蒂芬一起工作。但他和他一起给我发了几十封电子邮件，描绘了他们制造的设备。所以无论如何，这是一次真正的了解经历。我很遗憾地说，自这项研究完成以来，其中一些人已经去世。因此，我很遗憾地说，未来的霍金传记作者将无法接触到这些人。

paras.en: Kane: I did not realize he wasn’t a very diligent student. Like, young and in elementary school and, and what, you know, we Americans would refer to as, like, high school and early college years, he was not particularly interested in academics. It was boring. He was, you know, a bit of a gifted child syndrome. It was a little too easy for him, and he wasn’t really engaged, which is interesting because he was so popular. Like, he had friends. He was on the rowing team. He was busy tinkering with his friends and building helicopters and radios. It’s interesting to think about how that led to the popularized figure of Stephen Hawking that we have in our minds.
paras.zh: 凯恩：我没有意识到他不是一个非常勤奋的学生。比如，年轻的时候，在小学，以及，你知道，我们美国人所说的高中和大学早期，他对学术并不是特别感兴趣。很无聊。你知道，他有点天才儿童综合症。这对他来说有点太容易了，而且他并没有真正投入，这很有趣，因为他很受欢迎。就像，他有朋友。他是赛艇队的成员。他正忙着和朋友们一起修修补补，建造直升机和收音机。想想这如何导致了我们心目中斯蒂芬·霍金这个受欢迎的人物，这是很有趣的。

paras.en: Farmelo: Well, it could very easily have gone wrong. Remember, if you just move the focus along to when he was at college—he was at [the University of] Oxford—that, on the quiet, he’d registered for the Oxford Union, which trains prime ministers. And at the age of 17, he was debating in that society opposite a future prime minister at one point, right? But what he didn’t want to do was spend all the time being a swot. He knew he was good; he came very close not to getting the top grade because he was spending so much of his time partying and coxing.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：嗯，这很容易出错。请记住，如果你把焦点转移到他上大学时——他在牛津大学——你会发现，他悄悄地加入了培训首相的牛津联盟。 17 岁时，他曾经在那个社会与一位未来的首相辩论，对吗？但他不想做的就是一直当个傻瓜。他知道自己很好；他差一点就没有获得最高分，因为他花了太多时间参加派对和哄骗。

paras.en: But one thing that I cut from the book, and I perhaps shouldn’t have done, but Derek Powney, who sadly died a couple of years ago, I showed him a telegram that he sent Stephen Hawking, and it said something like this. This is pretty accurate. He said, “Congratulations. A first-class honors degree on one term’s work.” [Laughs] Now, I think that’s a little bit of an exaggeration, but do you see what he’s saying? That basically he only got his finger out, as they say in English English, right, in the last term because he was having such fun. And that could have been disastrous.
paras.zh: 但我从书中删去了一件事，也许我不应该做，但是几年前不幸去世的德里克·鲍尼，我给他看了一封他发给史蒂芬·霍金的电报，上面写着这样的话。这是相当准确的。他说：“恭喜你。一个学期的工作获得了一级荣誉学位。” [笑] 现在，我认为这有点夸张，但是你明白他在说什么吗？基本上，他只是在上学期伸出了手指，就像他们用英语说的那样，对吧，因为他玩得很开心。那可能是灾难性的。

paras.en: Kane: Yeah, so he was quite the mischievous child, and he was very popular and, as you said, was always going to parties, hosting parties. He had a very rich social life.
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的，所以他是一个非常顽皮的孩子，而且他很受欢迎，正如你所说，他总是去参加聚会，举办聚会。他的社交生活非常丰富。

paras.en: And he kept a secret during this time. He was considered maybe frail. He was known to his friends as maybe a bit clumsy. But it was also during this time that he was getting his first diagnosis of motor neurone disease.
paras.zh: 而他在这段时间里一直保守着一个秘密。人们认为他可能很虚弱。他的朋友们都知道他可能有点笨拙。但也正是在这段时间，他第一次被诊断出运动神经元疾病。

paras.en: Farmelo: That was just after he graduated from Oxford. He got into [the University of] Cambridge, and after one term, he got that diagnosis. Basically the upshot was that he would probably be dead within the next two or three years, at most five. Absolutely devastating for him, right? Although he didn’t show it particularly clearly, but also his parents and his sisters ...
paras.zh: 法梅洛：那是他从牛津大学毕业后不久。他进入了剑桥大学，一个学期后，他得到了这样的诊断。基本上结果就是他可能会在未来两三年内死去，最多五年。对他来说绝对是毁灭性的，对吧？虽然他没有表现得特别清楚，但还有他的父母和他的姐妹们……

paras.en: Kane: Yes, I mean, you had access to his father’s diaries at this time, and his father was very concerned, and this was very devastating news that Stephen might not have a future or what that future would look like. There’s a sentiment in the book at one point where Frank, Stephen’s father, is looking at the medical journals that he has access to at the time and looking into ...
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的，我的意思是，你当时可以看到他父亲的日记，他的父亲非常担心，这是一个非常毁灭性的消息，斯蒂芬可能没有未来，或者未来会是什么样子。书中有一种情绪，斯蒂芬的父亲弗兰克正在查看他当时可以访问的医学期刊并研究......

paras.en: Farmelo: And hiding them from his wife ...
paras.zh: 法梅洛：并且向他的妻子隐瞒了它们......

paras.en: Kane: Yes, and he hides them from his wife, and him and his wife do not tell Stephen right away. Stephen overhears a conversation.
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的，他对他的妻子隐瞒了这些，他和他的妻子没有立即告诉斯蒂芬。斯蒂芬无意中听到一段对话。

paras.en: Farmelo: Nobody told him. That’s exactly right. And even then, Stephen was in—it’s a pattern throughout his life—he was in denial. His mother would say, “He looks unperturbed.” And his father, you should read his diaries, right? One of them—I don’t think this is in the book ’cause my publishers didn’t like this, although I think they’ve changed their mind now—it begins, “Damn, damn, damn, damn.” And his father was saying, that he would walk into a room and burst into tears. It was a really terrible thing for his father, and his father worked his socks off to try and find if there was any hope, and it looked like there were none. Because that was a very primitive field in medicine. And basically there was nothing to be done.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：没人告诉他。完全正确。即便如此，史蒂芬仍然处于否认之中——这是他一生的一种模式。他的母亲会说：“他看起来很平静。”还有他的父亲，你应该看看他的日记，对吧？其中之一——我不认为这会出现在书中，因为我的出版商不喜欢这个，尽管我认为他们现在改变了主意——它的开头是“该死，该死，该死，该死。”他的父亲说，他会走进一个房间，放声大哭。这对他的父亲来说真是一件可怕的事情，他的父亲竭尽全力想看看是否还有希望，但看起来没有希望。因为那是医学中一个非常原始的领域。而且基本上没有什么可做的。

paras.en: Kane: Yeah, I mean, Stephen Hawking comes from two very loving parents who were very interested and very invested in his future. And then he gets this devastating diagnosis fairly early in his life, and it really throws all of their plans off track. And then as he grows—his disease is degenerative; it’s not exactly getting better with time, as they expected—and then he meets Jane [Wilde; later Jane Hawking], and him and Jane fall deeply in love. And this surprises his parents, it seemed. I mean, they had very real concerns about this relationship and if she really understood what her future with Stephen Hawking would be. But I have to say, one of the things I didn’t fully understand about Stephen Hawking’s personal life is the scandal around his marriages and his relationships with Jane. So can you just explain for our listeners, who maybe are not invested in the British tabloid press, what is exactly the relationship between Stephen, Jane, Jonathan [Hellyer Jones] and then, later on, Elaine [Mason]?
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的，我的意思是，斯蒂芬·霍金有两个非常慈爱的父母，他们对他的未来非常感兴趣并且非常投入。然后他很早就得到了这个毁灭性的诊断，这真的让他们所有的计划都偏离了轨道。然后，随着他的成长，他的疾病开始退化；随着时间的推移，情况并没有像他们预期的那样好转——然后他遇到了简[王尔德；后来的简·霍金]，他和简深深地相爱了。这似乎让他的父母感到惊讶。我的意思是，他们对这段关系非常担心，以及她是否真的了解她与史蒂芬·霍金的未来会是什么。但我不得不说，关于斯蒂芬·霍金的个人生活，我不完全了解的一件事是他的婚姻以及他与简的关系的丑闻。那么，您能否为我们的听众（他们可能不关心英国小报）解释一下斯蒂芬、简、乔纳森（赫利尔琼斯）以及后来的伊莱恩（梅森）之间到底是什么关系？

paras.en: Farmelo: First thing is that Stephen did have a girlfriend, right before Jane, and she ran away. She just couldn’t handle it. He’s never mentioned this to anybody else but his mother, and he, one of his sisters has seen this, right? He met Jane, and this was an extraordinary young woman because when she found out that he had this thing, she was shocked, but she just was not gonna let that stand between them.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：首先，斯蒂芬确实有一个女朋友，就在简之前，但她逃跑了。她就是受不了。除了他的母亲之外，他从未向任何人提起过这一点，而他，他的一个姐妹也看到了这一点，对吧？他遇到了简，这是一位非凡的年轻女子，因为当她发现他有这个东西时，她很震惊，但她不会让这成为他们之间的障碍。

paras.en: And as I say in the book, this is actually crucial in his life. Although the marriage lasted decades, the key thing was it gave him a reason why he had to earn some money. Wasn’t just a matter of passing his Ph.D.; he had to support, certainly, their life together. He was a bright graduate student, and then the great gravitational physicist Roger Penrose comes up with this discovery of how a sufficiently heavy star can actually collapse to form a singularity, which basically was the basis of modern black hole theory, right?
paras.zh: 正如我在书中所说，这实际上对他的生活至关重要。虽然这段婚姻持续了几十年，但关键是这给了他一个必须挣钱的理由。这不仅仅是通过博士学位的问题；当然，他必须支持他们共同的生活。他是一名聪明的研究生，然后伟大的引力物理学家罗杰·彭罗斯提出了一个发现，即一颗足够重的恒星实际​​上如何塌缩形成奇点，这基本上是现代黑洞理论的基础，对吗？

paras.en: Now, that was a major research discovery, right? Stephen, very bright, that supercharged his research interest. So do you see he had this wonderful rebirth, so to speak, right? He’d met a great love who he was desperate to marry. His research was going well, right? But Stephen’s parents on the side were saying, with a lot of admiration for Jane, but “Does she really know what is happening?” Stephen and Jane looked away basically, said, “We can handle this.” You know, it’s admirable in some ways but terrifying for Stephen’s parents.
paras.zh: 现在，这是一项重大研究发现，对吗？斯蒂芬非常聪明，这激发了他的研究兴趣。那么你看到他有这么美妙的重生吗？可以这么说，对吗？他遇到了一位他渴望结婚的伟大爱情。他的研究进展顺利，对吗？但斯蒂芬的父母在一旁对简充满钦佩地说，“她真的知道发生了什么事吗？”斯蒂芬和简基本上移开了视线，说道：“我们可以处理这件事。”你知道，这在某些方面令人钦佩，但对斯蒂芬的父母来说却很可怕。

paras.en: For the first few years, Stephen’s work was progressing well. They got accommodation courtesy of one of the Cambridge colleges, and everything appeared to be going well. But his condition was going to get worse, and it did. And one of the big strains on the relationship was that Stephen was a very difficult patient. Most people could put theirselves into Jane’s shoes and see that, you know, his selfishness as she saw it, in, you know, pursuing his academic career and not being a compliant patient—husband, right? It really got to her. It became a really heavy burden for her. I’m oversimplifying, but, in Stephen’s words, they grew apart
paras.zh: 最初几年，斯蒂芬的工作进展顺利。他们得到了剑桥大学一所学院提供的住宿，一切似乎都很顺利。但他的病情会变得更糟，而且确实如此。这段关系的最大压力之一是斯蒂芬是一个非常难相处的病人。大多数人都可以设身处地为简着想，在她看来，他的自私是在追求学术生涯而不是做一个顺从的病人——丈夫，对吧？这确实对她产生了影响。这对她来说确实是一个沉重的负担。我过于简单化了，但是，用斯蒂芬的话来说，他们渐行渐远

paras.en: Kane: I mean, I would imagine the change of relationship between newlywed and new wife into a caregiver would dramatically change their personal relationship, I’ll say. And, and this is seen through the invitation of Jonathan into their lives.
paras.zh: 凯恩：我的意思是，我会说，我认为新婚夫妇和新妻子之间的关系转变为照顾者将极大地改变他们的个人关系。这一点可以从乔纳森邀请他们进入他们的生活中看出。

paras.en: Farmelo: Yeah. Well, Jane was under enormous stress—she said this in her own book—really concerned for her children. He fathered three children, which was a wonderful thing for him and for her. But still this, of course, made her responsible for so many things in that house. She was becoming very lonely and really [at] her wit’s end about how to deal with this. And she met somebody whose wife had recently died, and that was Jonathan. And they became close, eventually intimate, right? And, far as she could see, Stephen didn’t mind this.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：是的。嗯，简承受着巨大的压力——她在自己的书中这样说——非常关心她的孩子。他生了三个孩子，这对他和她来说都是一件美妙的事情。但当然，这仍然让她对房子里的很多事情负责。她变得非常孤独，对于如何处理这个问题真的束手无策。她遇到了一个妻子最近去世的人，那就是乔纳森。他们变得很亲密，最终变得亲密，对吗？而且，据她所知，斯蒂芬并不介意这一点。

paras.en: Kane: Yes, I mean, he’s quoted at one point as, “As long as they are discreet.”
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的，我的意思是，他曾一度被引用为“只要他们谨慎”。

paras.en: Farmelo: Well, that’s what, that’s her report. Jane’s perfectly entitled to say that, and I take that on. But Stephen has never said this. He told friends that he was very unhappy about this. She says she saw no sign of this. I wasn’t there, so I simply have to present things as they were, right? Incidentally, I’ve met Jonathan. I think he’s the most lovely man. Now, I don’t think you need to be a complete macho person to say that having your wife’s “friend,” in inverted commas, staying in your house, right, and taking this role was not exactly Stephen’s comfort zone. I’m being very, very discreet here, alright? And this is the point where Stephen’s eyes started looking elsewhere, and that’s when he fell for one of his nurses, Elaine.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：嗯，就是这样，这就是她的报告。简完全有资格这么说，我也同意这一点。但史蒂芬从来没有说过这样的话。他告诉朋友，他对此非常不满。她说她没有看到任何迹象。我不在场，所以我只能按原样呈现，对吧？顺便说一句，我见过乔纳森。我认为他是最可爱的人。现在，我认为你不需要成为一个十足的男子气概的人，才能说拥有你妻子的“朋友”（用引号引起来），住在你的房子里，对吧，并且担任这个角色并不完全是斯蒂芬的舒适区。我在这里非常非常谨慎，好吗？就在这时，斯蒂芬的目光开始转向别处，就在那时，他爱上了他的一位护士伊莱恩。

paras.en: And that was a horrible period of—you can imagine, right? Because he and Jane end up divorcing, and after a period, he married Elaine. That was terrible for him because he didn’t want all this stuff going public, and it did. And the newspapers were reporting on it. Jane wrote a book about it, which was very graphic. So this stuff is pretty, pretty tough to read. But I took the view, as far as I possibly could, of presenting all sides of the story.
paras.zh: 那是一段可怕的时期——你可以想象，对吧？因为他和简最终离婚了，一段时间后，他娶了伊莱恩。这对他来说很糟糕，因为他不想让所有这些东西公开，而事实确实如此。报纸对此进行了报道。简写了一本关于它的书，非常生动。所以这些东西很漂亮，但很难读。但我尽可能地呈现故事的各个方面。

paras.en: Kane: Yes, I mean, it was years of personal dramas being reported in the tabloids and, and a lot of very inappropriate questions being asked of people about the personal relationships between them. But at this time, there’s also very serious accusations coming from Stephen’s children, as well as coming from other nurses, that Elaine was abusive in some capacity. Is it your understanding that Elaine was abusive?
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的，我的意思是，小报上报道了多年来的个人戏剧，并且向人们提出了很多关于他们之间的私人关系的非常不恰当的问题。但此时，斯蒂芬的孩子以及其他护士也提出了非常严重的指控，称伊莱恩在某种程度上存在虐待行为。你认为伊莱恩有虐待行为吗？

paras.en: Farmelo: That statement has never been validated within a legal environment. The police investigated this twice.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：这一说法从未在法律环境中得到验证。警方曾两次对此进行调查。

paras.en: Kane: Yes, and Stephen also never has said publicly that there was any maltreatment in that relationship, but his children and the other nurses were concerned and, and voiced this concern to him on multiple occasions.
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的，斯蒂芬也从未公开表示这种关系中存在任何虐待，但他的孩子和其他护士对此表示担忧，并多次向他表达了这种担忧。

paras.en: Farmelo: It is a difficult thing to report on, right? Because all the different parties will read my account and say, “Well, that’s not what I saw.” But my job was to present, as far as I can, the different sides so that readers can decide. But I’ll tell you one thing: I never saw a single line where he criticized either of his wives. But he did do one thing. He said he was furious about the way that Elaine was treated by the press, right? That’s the one thing he said, right?
paras.zh: 法梅洛：报道起来很困难，对吧？因为所有各方都会读到我的叙述并说：“好吧，这不是我所看到的。”但我的工作是尽我所能地呈现不同的一面，以便读者可以做出决定。但我要告诉你一件事：我从未见过他批评他的妻子的任何一句话。但他确实做了一件事。他说他对媒体对待伊莱恩的方式感到愤怒，对吧？这就是他说的一件事，对吗？

paras.en: Kane: Yeah, I mean, he was not interested in being a celebrity that had their personal lives discussed openly in the British tabloids. He wanted to be a famous scientist. He wanted to talk about the science.
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的，我的意思是，他对成为英国小报公开讨论其个人生活的名人不感兴趣。他想成为一名著名的科学家。他想谈谈科学。

paras.en: Can you summarize Stephen Hawking’s physics contributions? I mean, how can you even say it? He’s contributed so much to the field. It’s hard to really summarize his influence on it. But can you please give me a summary today?
paras.zh: 您能总结一下斯蒂芬·霍金的物理学贡献吗？我的意思是，你怎么能这么说呢？他为这个领域做出了很多贡献。很难真正概括他对此的影响。但你今天能给我一个总结吗？

paras.en: Farmelo: I’ve spoken to dozens of world-leading scientists, right? people who are Stephen’s peers, right at the top of the Nobel- [and] Breakthrough Prize–winning, group of physicists, right? And it’s completely clear that they regard him as a truly great scientist, right? This notion that he’s only famous because he was disabled is a nonsense as far as they’re concerned.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：我已经和数十位世界领先的科学家交谈过，对吧？他们是斯蒂芬的同辈人，是诺贝尔突破奖获得者物理学家群体中的佼佼者，对吧？很明显，他们认为他是一位真正伟大的科学家，对吧？在他们看来，他只是因为残疾而出名的想法是无稽之谈。

paras.en: Farmelo: He did a lot of stuff. The main highlight that many people know about, but it’s worth stressing how great a contribution this was and how much it’s esteemed by his colleagues, and that is the nature of black holes.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：他做了很多事情。这是很多人都知道的主要亮点，但值得强调的是，这是一个多么伟大的贡献，以及他的同事们对它的尊重，这就是黑洞的本质。

paras.en: When he went into this field, there were plenty of people that didn’t believe in them. That’s really important to bear in mind. He wasn’t analyzing something he could look at and do experiments on. He was looking at something that emerged from Einstein’s equations of gravity. So that was a courageous thing to do. He wasn’t alone in doing it, but he invested, most of the time in the 1970s, to focus his prodigious energies into understanding these black holes.
paras.zh: 当他进入这个领域时，有很多人不相信他们。记住这一点非常重要。他并不是在分析一些他可以观察和做实验的东西。他正在研究从爱因斯坦引力方程中得出的东西。所以这是一件勇敢的事情。他并不是唯一一个这样做的人，但他在 20 世纪 70 年代的大部分时间里都投入了巨大的精力来了解这些黑洞。

paras.en: A black hole is a domain of space and time where—there is a boundary to it. Anything can fall into it, but once inside, nothing can get out, even light. For that reason, it’s a black hole, and it’s gravity that keeps even light within its boundaries. Now, what are the laws governing the behavior of that, right? Now, Stephen was one of the great pioneers of discovering those laws, and his tour de force, which he did in late 1973—and I want to point out here, at that time, his good friend Martin Rees thought he was dying, right? He was going into Stephen’s office thinking, “I don’t think Stephen’s gonna last another year.”
paras.zh: 黑洞是一个空间和时间的域，它有一个边界。任何东西都可能掉进去，但一旦进去，就没有任何东西可以出来，甚至是光。因此，它是一个黑洞，并且它的引力使光也保持在其边界内。现在，管理这种行为的法律是什么，对吧？现在，斯蒂芬是发现这些定律的伟大先驱之一，也是他在 1973 年底所做的杰作——我想在这里指出，当时，他的好朋友马丁·里斯 (Martin Rees) 以为他快要死了，对吗？他走进斯蒂芬的办公室时心里想：“我认为斯蒂芬撑不了一年了。”

paras.en: And Stephen, then, was doing one of the great calculations of 20th-century physics. What is that calculation? He was looking at the behavior of quanta, of tiny subatomic particles on the outside that boundary of a black hole in what we call curved spacetime. And he showed that if you introduce quantum theory—that’s the theory of the very, very small that we have to use when we look at atoms or molecules—if you apply that to black hole theory, then, in a absolute tour de force calculation, it demonstrates that black holes must be radiating. They are not completely black.
paras.zh: 当时，斯蒂芬正在进行 20 世纪物理学中一项伟大的计算。那算什么？他正在研究量子的行为，即我们所说的弯曲时空中黑洞边界外部的微小亚原子粒子的行为。他表明，如果你引入量子理论——这是我们在观察原子或分子时必须使用的非常非常小的理论——如果你将其应用于黑洞理论，那么，在绝对的杰作计算中，它证明黑洞一定是在辐射的。它们并不是完全黑色的。

paras.en: Let me just say to you that when I was shown by a real expert how to do that calculation, the expert said four times to me, “If I were doing that calculation, I would’ve given up four times,” alright? It is absolutely prodigious. He did that calculation, as far as I can tell, in about five or six weeks.
paras.zh: 让我告诉你，当一位真正的专家向我展示如何进行该计算时，专家对我说了四次，“如果我进行该计算，我会放弃四次，”好吗？这绝对是惊人的。据我所知，他大约花了五六周的时间完成了这个计算。

paras.en: Early 1974 it broke, and when he announced it, the chairman of the seminar [where] he gave it said, “Well, this is obviously nonsense.” And it took another, I think, six, seven months before the overwhelming majority of his peer group actually accepted what he’d done. So this wasn’t just doing a quick calculation that other people can do, you know, in their coffee break. This was a major project, right? And that still, right, still is the subject of researchers today. They are still looking, trying to understand the behavior of black holes in detail with Stephen Hawking’s contribution at the heart of it. He did lots of other things, but that is the thing he will always be remembered for, for sure.
paras.zh: 1974 年初，它破裂了，当他宣布这一消息时，他举办的研讨会的主席说：“嗯，这显然是无稽之谈。”我想，又过了六、七个月，他的同龄人中的绝大多数才真正接受了他的所作所为。所以这不仅仅是做其他人在喝咖啡休息时可以做的快速计算。这是一个重大项目，对吗？这仍然是今天研究人员的主题。他们仍在寻找，试图详细了解黑洞的行为，并以史蒂芬·霍金的贡献为核心。他还做了很多其他事情，但这肯定是他将永远被人们铭记的事情。

paras.en: Kane: I wanted to brag about Scientific American a little bit for a moment because, as you say, in the early ’70s, he’s working on his, I will say, most famous work as a physicist, and in 1977 he writes a little article for a magazine you might have heard of, Scientific American.
paras.zh: 凯恩：我想暂时夸一下《科学美国人》，因为正如你所说，在 70 年代初，他正在研究他作为物理学家最著名的作品，1977 年他为一本你可能听说过的杂志《科学美国人》写了一篇小文章。

paras.en: Farmelo: Hold on, that’s wrong. It was a good article, right? In a very prominent magazine. [Laughs.] No, seriously, and it was a good article.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：等等，这是错误的。这是一篇好文章，对吧？在一本非常著名的杂志上。 [笑]不，说真的，这是一篇好文章。

paras.en: Kane: Yes. I mean, you say that this article really changed the trajectory of his field because not only was he brilliant, but he could articulate himself well to the masses. You didn’t have to have a Ph.D. in physics to understand Stephen Hawking talking to you about physics, which is an extraordinary skill.
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的。我的意思是，你说这篇文章确实改变了他的领域的轨迹，因为他不仅才华横溢，而且能够很好地向大众表达自己。你不必拥有博士学位。在物理学中理解斯蒂芬·霍金与你谈论物理学，这是一项非凡的技能。

paras.en: Farmelo: It is. Fred Hoyle, the great cosmologist, he was a predecessor of Stephen’s, one of Stephen’s idols when he was young. And he did a bit of popularization on the side. So Stephen had that as a precedent. So he decided to just try his hand. And as you rightly say, he did, wrote a very nice article for Scientific American. It was picked up by encyclopedias and other people started to pick this up. So he started to just dip his toes, so to speak, in celebrity stuff in the late ’70s.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：是的。弗莱德·霍伊尔，伟大的宇宙学家，他是斯蒂芬的前辈，是斯蒂芬年轻时的偶像之一。他还做了一些普及工作。所以斯蒂芬有这样的先例。所以他决定尝试一下。正如你所说，他确实为《科学美国人》写了一篇非常好的文章。它被百科全书收录，其他人也开始收录。因此，他在 70 年代末开始涉足名人事物。

paras.en: But that led to something very important, which is his incredible book, A Brief History of Time, which followed actually giving some lectures at Harvard University. When he saw the reception that his talk gave, he thought, “I’m gonna try and write a popular book.”
paras.zh: 但这导致了一些非常重要的事情，那就是他令人难以置信的书《时间简史》，随后在哈佛大学进行了一些讲座。当他看到自己的演讲受到热烈欢迎时，他想：“我要尝试写一本受欢迎的书。”

paras.en: And it took him a long time to do. It’s sold, we’re told, more than 25 million copies, about just the sheer wonder of living in this universe where you have these deep equations that you are investigating and making deductions from—understanding the nature of space and time, the nature of gravity, right? And he really was able to communicate that very well, both as a writer and indeed as a speaker—because, by that time, he had an artificial voice, by 1988.
paras.zh: 他花了很长时间才做到。据我们所知，这本书已售出超过 2500 万册，讲述了生活在这个宇宙中的纯粹奇迹，在这个宇宙中，你可以研究这些深刻的方程并从中进行推论——了解空间和时间的本质，重力的本质，对吗？他确实能够很好地表达这一点，无论是作为一名作家还是作为一名演讲者——因为到了 1988 年，他已经有了人工声音。

paras.en: Kane: Okay, I have to close this out today ’cause I could stay here and talk to you about this book for the rest of the day. But I wanted to ask you: Writing a biography about Stephen Hawking is an extraordinary task to take on as an author. He was a brilliant physicist. He is arguably one of the most popular authors of popular science writing. I mean, as you mentioned, A Brief History of Time was a yearlong New York Times bestseller, and that’s extraordinary feat just by itself. So at the end of the day, Graham, do you think he’d like your book?
paras.zh: 凯恩：好吧，我今天必须结束这个话题，因为我可以留在这里和你谈论这本书。但我想问你：作为一名作家，写一本关于史蒂芬·霍金的传记是一项非凡的任务。他是一位杰出的物理学家。他可以说是最受欢迎的科普作家之一。我的意思是，正如您提到的，《时间简史》是《纽约时报》长达一年的畅销书，这本身就是非凡的壮举。所以归根结底，格雷厄姆，你认为他会喜欢你的书吗？

paras.en: Farmelo: I hope he would. [Laughs.] I’d be very disappointed after six years researching if he didn’t. But I tell you one thing, I was always mindful, when writing it, to be fair to him. I want to make sure it’s grounded in the best factual information I have and in the widest possible input of views, right? And Stephen’s friends, they’ve been nice enough to say that I do capture that sense of this astonishing vitality and determination and stubbornness. And I hope I brought that across, and I hope you for one enjoyed it.
paras.zh: 法梅洛：我希望他会。 [笑]如果他不这样做，经过六年的研究，我会非常失望。但我告诉你一件事，我在写的时候总是很注意，要对他公平。我想确保它以我所拥有的最佳事实信息和尽可能广泛的观点为基础，对吗？斯蒂芬的朋友们很友善地说，我确实捕捉到了这种令人惊叹的活力、决心和固执的感觉。我希望我能传达这一点，也希望你们喜欢它。

paras.en: Kane: I definitely enjoyed it. Thank you so much, Graham.
paras.zh: 凯恩：我绝对喜欢它。非常感谢你，格雷厄姆。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s all for today’s episode. On Friday we’ll be revisiting one of our favorite episodes from the year while we chow down on leftovers, and we’re taking Monday off. We’ll be back with something fresh next Wednesday.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这就是今天这一集的全部内容。周五，我们将一边吃剩菜一边重温这一年中我们最喜欢的一集，周一休息。下周三我们会带着新鲜的东西回来。

paras.en: For Scientific American’s Science Quickly, I’m Rachel Feltman. Happy Thanksgiving!
paras.zh: 我是《科学美国人》的《科学快报》的雷切尔·费尔特曼。感恩节快乐！

articles.title: How the Galileo musical’s composer sets science to a score on Broadway

paras.en: What must it have been like to put your eye to the first Galilean telescope? A new musical on Broadway depicts the experience as absolutely electric—with a swelling chorus and pumped-up rock sound blaring while stars shine all around the audience.
paras.zh: 当你看到第一台伽利略望远镜时，会是什么样的感觉？百老汇的一部新音乐剧将这种体验描述为绝对震撼人心的体验——伴随着激昂的合唱和震耳欲聋的摇滚乐，而星星在观众周围闪耀。

paras.en: Galileo is a new Broadway musical opening on December 6. It tells the story of pioneering astronomer Galileo Galilei and the way that his public support for the heliocentric view of the universe sparked conflict with the Catholic Church. The show’s ballads depict how the Church hobbled Galileo’s efforts to advance astronomy, but it also makes it clear that he was both a man of faith and a rebellious soul. (The sometimes Christian rock–like melodies and lyrics also support this aspect of the character.) The show doesn’t shy away from the complications of Galileo’s conflict with the church, propelled by his close friendship with Bishop Maffeo Barberini, who later, as pope, played a key role in forcing Galileo to recant and sentencing him to house arrest for teaching heliocentrism.
paras.zh: 《伽利略》是一部将于 12 月 6 日上演的新百老汇音乐剧。它讲述了天文学家先驱伽利略·伽利雷的故事，以及他对日心说宇宙观的公开支持如何引发了与天主教会的冲突。该剧的歌谣描述了教会如何阻碍伽利略推进天文学的努力，但也清楚地表明他既是一个有信仰的人，也是一个叛逆的灵魂。 （有时基督教摇滚般的旋律和歌词也支持了这个角色的这一方面。）该剧并没有回避伽利略与教会冲突的复杂性，这是由于他与主教马菲奥·巴贝里尼（Maffeo Barberini）的亲密友谊所推动的，后者在后来担任教皇期间，在迫使伽利略放弃信仰并因教导日心说而判处他软禁方面发挥了关键作用。

paras.en: Galileo’s music, lyrics and arrangements were created by composers Michael Weiner and Zoe Sarnak. Once it opens, Sarnak will be focusing her creative attention as composer of two more STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics)–themed musicals: Particle Fever, an adaptation of a 2013 documentary about the discovery of the Higgs boson with the same title, and a stage adaptation of the film A Beautiful Mind. “I’m in my science era, I like to joke,” she says. “And I’m thrilled about it.”
paras.zh: 伽利略的音乐、歌词和编曲均由作曲家迈克尔·韦纳和佐伊·萨尔纳克创作。演出结束后，萨纳克将集中精力创作另外两部 STEM（科学、技术、工程和数学）主题音乐剧：《粒子狂热》，改编自 2013 年一部关于发现希格斯玻色子的同名纪录片，以及根据电影《美丽心灵》改编的舞台剧。 “我处于科学时代，我喜欢开玩笑，”她说。 “我对此感到兴奋。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Scientific American spoke to Sarnak about how sound tells Galileo’s story in the new musical, how she puts science to a soundtrack and why this story is ripe for a retelling today.
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》采访了萨纳克，讲述了声音如何在新音乐剧中讲述伽利略的故事，她如何将科学融入到配乐中，以及为什么这个故事现在适合重述。

paras.en: [An edited transcript of the conversation follows.]
paras.zh: [经过编辑的谈话记录如下。]

paras.en: You studied science before you decided to become a composer. How did your research experience fuel your music?
paras.zh: 在你决定成为一名作曲家之前你学习了科学。您的研究经历如何推动您的音乐发展？

paras.en: I would say, if you asked kids from my high school what they thought I was going to be when I grew up, they would say a mathematician or a scientist. My dad is a mathematician, my mom studied philosophy... She does ethics of technology at Cornell Tech. I took music as something I did for fun..., because I’ve been composing music since I was very young. But I have a family of professors and doctors, so that’s sort of the family trade, you know? So I was doing molecular bio and music in parallel in my undergrad. I worked in a virology lab, and it was a huge part of my life.
paras.zh: 我想说，如果你问我高中的孩子们他们认为我长大后会做什么，他们会说数学家或科学家。我的父亲是一名数学家，我的母亲学习哲学……她在康奈尔理工大学研究技术伦理学。我把音乐当作一种乐趣……因为我从很小的时候就开始创作音乐。但我有一个由教授和医生组成的家庭，所以这就是家族生意，你知道吗？所以我在本科时同时研究分子生物和音乐。我在病毒学实验室工作，这是我生活的重要组成部分。

paras.en: I think there’s a relationship between [molecular biology and music] in thinking in a map-based way and integrating layers of information, as opposed to just one linear thought. When you think about music and how it works, as a composer, you're thinking melody, harmony, rhythmic structures, counterpoints, how they all come together. And I think that the puzzle that is, for example, molecular bio is kind of similar in that way.
paras.zh: 我认为[分子生物学和音乐]在基于地图的思维方式和整合信息层之间存在着某种关系，而不仅仅是一种线性思维。当你思考音乐及其运作方式时，作为作曲家，你会思考旋律、和声、节奏结构、对位法，以及它们如何组合在一起。我认为分子生物之谜在这方面有点相似。

paras.en: What has been cool about this moment as I come into writing Galileo and Particle Fever is: I can actually explore the emotion behind what these scientists go through. The soul of a scientist sings to me because of the dreamer quality, because of the creative, thinking-outside-the-box quality. If Sunday in the Park with George makes sense as a musical, then certainly Galileo does.
paras.zh: 当我开始写《伽利略》和《粒子狂热》时，最酷的时刻是：我可以真正探索这些科学家所经历的事情背后的情感。科学家的灵魂向我歌唱，因为他有梦想家的品质，因为有创造力、跳出框框思考的品质。如果《周日与乔治在公园》作为一部音乐剧有意义，那么《伽利略》当然也有意义。

paras.en: He was this kind of rebellious figure speaking truth to power. And when [Weiner and I] started to talk about it, it felt useful to imagine that he’s a rock star because of that. And suddenly, you can feel how explosive he is, how brave he is, how unbridled and brash he is, which, by the way, he was. Like the actual Galileo was certainly not a meek man. And I remember thinking about the way [punk musician] Patti Smith talks about using music to speak truth to power. And it’s like, if there's a lens for this person’s story to be told, it’s through rock music.
paras.zh: 他就是这种向权力讲真话的叛逆人物。当[韦纳和我]开始谈论这件事时，想象他因此而成为摇滚明星感觉很有用。突然间，你能感觉到他是多么的爆发力，他是多么的勇敢，他是多么的肆无忌惮和傲慢，顺便说一句，他确实是这样。就像真正的伽利略一样，他当然不是一个温顺的人。我记得想到[朋克音乐家]帕蒂·史密斯谈论用音乐向权力说出真相的方式。就像，如果有一个镜头可以讲述这个人的故事，那就是通过摇滚音乐。

paras.en: It makes sense once you start working on something like this and you see how much people have engaged with his story through the years in various art forms because the stakes are so high and it’s evergreen in its relevance, for better or worse, because we’re constantly coming up against moments where a new way of thinking hits up against the power structure. That’s part of the ebbs and flows of how civilization works. And so that got me really excited about a way in which we could tell this story that can only be told through a musical, theatrically.
paras.zh: 一旦你开始从事这样的事情，你会发现多年来有多少人以各种艺术形式参与到他的故事中，这是有道理的，因为赌注如此之高，而且它的相关性是常青的，无论好坏，因为我们不断遇到新的思维方式与权力结构发生冲突的时刻。这是文明运作方式潮起潮落的一部分。因此，这让我对我们能够讲述这个只能通过音乐剧、戏剧来讲述的故事的方式感到非常兴奋。

paras.en: I heard that you wanted to have each character in Galileo’s story have a distinct musical sound. Can you describe what they are and why?
paras.zh: 我听说您想让伽利略故事中的每个角色都有独特的音乐声音。你能描述一下它们是什么以及为什么吗？

paras.en: Starting with Galileo, we were really interested in a version of his sound that feels sort of [like] rebellious, unbridled rock. He’s pushing against a system that doesn’t want to let a new idea come into the light, and so he has to explode against it. That felt very clear. He still has a lot of depth emotionally, and we do have moments where he’s quite quiet, but those tend to be personal, with Barberini or with his daughter Virginia. But to capture the sound of what it would mean to see the [celestial bodies] that no one had seen..., that would be like a “hits you in your core” kind of experience. So we knew we wanted that for him.
paras.zh: 从伽利略开始，我们对他的声音版本非常感兴趣，感觉有点像叛逆、肆无忌惮的摇滚乐。他正在反对一个不想让新想法曝光的制度，所以他必须爆发反对它。那感觉非常清楚。他在情感上仍然有很多深度，我们确实有他非常安静的时刻，但那些往往是私人的，与巴贝里尼或他的女儿弗吉尼亚在一起。但要捕捉到看到从未见过的[天体]意味着什么的声音……，那就像是一种“击中你的核心”的体验。所以我们知道我们希望他能做到这一点。

paras.en: With his daughter Virginia, then, we were thinking about how his real daughter had wisdom and soulfulness to her. She was born into a very difficult circumstance, and yet their correspondence shows that she was very brilliant as well, [with] an ability not to be toppled by a system that was really quite stacked against her. But she has a younger sound purposefully. We want her to start in the space of hopeful the way that teenagers are and then evolve into the version of her that is in Act II.
paras.zh: 然后，和他的女儿弗吉尼亚一起，我们思考他真正的女儿如何拥有智慧和深情。她出生在一个非常困难的环境中，但他们的信件表明她也非常聪明，有能力不被一个对她不利的制度推翻。但她故意让声音听起来更年轻。我们希望她像青少年一样从充满希望的空间开始，然后演变成第二幕中的她。

paras.en: I think with the pope, we use a lot of strings but strings in this chamber way that sounds influenced by music in mass—a chamber classical element to the church sound. Barberini has a beauty to what he sings, but he pulls it in a modern direction. Until you get to what happens in Act II, he’s a progressive thinker within the realm of the church, which helped us shape his sound.
paras.zh: 我认为对于教皇，我们使用了很多弦乐，但弦乐以这种室内乐的方式听起来受到了大众音乐的影响——教堂声音的室内乐古典元素。巴贝里尼的歌声很美，但他把它推向了现代的方向。在你了解第二幕中发生的事情之前，他是教会领域内的一位进步思想家，这帮助我们塑造了他的声音。

paras.en: Can you preview some musical choices you made for Particle Fever?
paras.zh: 你能预览一下你为《粒子狂热》所做的一些音乐选择吗？

paras.en: Galileo sits at the intersection of a scientist and his dreams and the political circumstance and how those explode against one another, whereas Particle Fever is zoomed in. It’s set at CERN, and we’re asking people to dive into the importance of discovering the Higgs boson. It’s a whole world of physics that we have to immerse people in. Because particle physics speaks to the tiny and also, therefore, the origins of the universe—the infinite—it has a scope of pointillism up to massive orchestral gestures. And that’s really exciting, musically, for me because it lets these two shows have very different sound worlds.
paras.zh: 《伽利略》处于一位科学家、他的梦想、政治环境以及这些因素如何相互爆发的交汇处，而《粒子狂热》则被放大。它以欧洲核子研究中心为背景，我们要求人们深入探讨发现希格斯玻色子的重要性。这是一个我们必须让人们沉浸其中的物理世界。因为粒子物理学涉及微小，因此也涉及宇宙的起源——无限——它的范围从点画派到巨大的管弦乐手势。从音乐上来说，这对我来说真的很令人兴奋，因为它让这两部剧拥有了截然不同的声音世界。

paras.en: I think that the shared thing is definitely the humanity that lives inside of our desire to explore and progress. For Particle Fever, there’s this question of whether or not those kinds of projects will be funded moving forward and whether we, as a civilization, commit to the importance of discovery. So a big part of Particle Fever is saying, “This is core to who we are as people.”
paras.zh: 我认为共同的东西绝对是生活在我们探索和进步的愿望之中的人性。对于粒子狂热来说，存在这样的问题：此类项目是否会得到资助，以及我们作为一个文明是否致力于发现的重要性。因此，《粒子狂热》的很大一部分内容是说：“这是我们作为人的核心。”

paras.en: Why should science stories be told on Broadway right now?
paras.zh: 为什么现在应该在百老汇讲述科学故事？

paras.en: As a composer and a writer, it’s important to make things that are beautiful, but it’s also important to know you have something to say about the world outside of your art form. And I feel honored that I have an opportunity to advocate for research, science and the progress that comes when we follow the intuition and the rigor of the human mind, things that I took for granted because of my context growing up, and now I feel it’s a duty to fight for them.
paras.zh: 作为一名作曲家和作家，创作美丽的东西很重要，但知道你对艺术形式之外的世界有话要说也很重要。我感到很荣幸，我有机会倡导研究、科学以及当我们遵循人类思维的直觉和严谨时所带来的进步，这些事情由于我的成长环境而被我认为是理所当然的，现在我觉得有责任为它们而奋斗。

paras.en: I think it is very clear that we are in a time where the questions [are] “What is truth? How do we advocate for progress?” Those questions are very much on my mind and all of our minds. That is why I think [Galileo, especially] is wildly relevant today.
paras.zh: 我认为很明显，我们正处于一个问题是“什么是真理？我们如何倡导进步？”的时代。这些问题一直困扰着我和我们所有人。这就是为什么我认为[尤其是伽利略]在今天非常重要。

articles.title: This year’s El Niño is unlike any other on record
articles.author: Nikk Ogasa

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: It was an unprecedented year for El Niño, the weather-changing ocean pattern defined by warmer-than-normal surface waters in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. By October 18, the ocean area that researchers use to monitor El Niño’s severity climbed to an average temperature of over 30° Celsius (86° Fahrenheit) for the first time in history. From there, it kept on rising.
paras.zh: 对于厄尔尼诺现象来说，今年是史无前例的一年，厄尔尼诺现象是一种改变天气的海洋模式，其特征是赤道太平洋中部和东部的地表水温高于正常水平。到 10 月 18 日，研究人员用来监测厄尔尼诺现象严重程度的海域平均温度历史上首次攀升至 30 摄氏度（86 华氏度）以上。从那时起，它继续上涨。

paras.en: In September, the region’s daily average sea surface temperature reached the most extreme level ever recorded: more than 3.03 degrees Celsius above the 30-year average (dashed line). The World Meteorological Organization predicts that sea surface temperatures may peak at 3.7 degrees above that average by January. The two previous strongest El Niños on record emerged in 1997 and 2015.
paras.zh: 9月，该地区日平均海面温度达到有记录以来的最极端水平：比30年平均水平（虚线）高出3.03摄氏度以上。世界气象组织预测，到 1 月份，海面温度可能会达到峰值，比平均水平高出 3.7 度。有记录以来前两次最强的厄尔尼诺现象分别出现在 1997 年和 2015 年。

paras.en: All that hot water has fueled the most active Pacific hurricane season on record. By mid-October, 331 units of cyclone energy had accumulated, beating out 2018’s record of 318 units. It has also unleashed heat into the atmosphere, affecting distant circulation patterns and leading to an extraordinarily quiet Atlantic hurricane season.
paras.zh: 所有这些热水都助长了有记录以来最活跃的太平洋飓风季节。截至 10 月中旬，旋风能量已累积 331 单位，打破了 2018 年 318 单位的记录。它还向大气中释放热量，影响遥远的环流模式，导致大西洋飓风季节异常安静。

paras.en: 2026’s El Niño will be felt well beyond the New Year. Precipitation and drought impacts are expected across the world through spring 2027. And the global heating effect could compound with human-caused climate warming to make 2027 the hottest year ever recorded.
paras.zh: 2026 年的厄尔尼诺现象在新年之后仍将存在。预计到 2027 年春季，全球都会遭受降水和干旱影响。全球变暖效应可能与人为造成的气候变暖相结合，使 2027 年成为有记录以来最热的一年。

paras.en: The heat that El Niño unleashes into the atmosphere shifts storm tracks and weather patterns globally. Here are some of the most significant observed and anticipated effects.
paras.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象释放到大气中的热量改变了全球风暴路径和天气模式。以下是一些最显着的观察到和预期的影响。

articles.title: ‘Mitt & Ted’ recounts how a political odd couple changed U.S. health care
articles.author: Lily Burton

paras.en: In 1973, U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy often visited the cancer ward at Boston Children’s Hospital, where his eldest son was battling osteosarcoma. Kennedy witnessed other parents on the ward make impossible decisions regarding their child’s care when insurance didn’t cover it. Their stories lit a fire within the senator that burned bright for the rest of his life.
paras.zh: 1973年，美国参议员特德·肯尼迪经常探访波士顿儿童医院的癌症病房，他的大儿子正在那里与骨肉瘤作斗争。肯尼迪亲眼目睹了病房里的其他父母在保险不承保的情况下就孩子的护理做出了不可能的决定。他们的故事点燃了这位参议员内心的火焰，并在他的余生中熊熊燃烧。

paras.en: Kennedy spent decades fighting for health care reform, representing his home state of Massachusetts. He even teamed up with a former political rival from across the aisle: Mitt Romney. The story of this unexpected alliance is recounted in Mitt & Ted, the newest season of the GBH News podcast The Big Dig. Over eight episodes, journalist and host Ian Coss explores how their work laid the foundation for the Affordable Care Act, one of the most significant and divisive health care reforms in U.S. history.
paras.zh: 肯尼迪花了几十年时间代表他的家乡马萨诸塞州争取医疗改革。他甚至与来自两党的前政治对手米特·罗姆尼(Mitt Romney)合作。 GBH 新闻播客 The Big Dig 的最新一季《Mitt & Ted》讲述了这一意外联盟的故事。在八集中，记者兼主持人伊恩·科斯探讨了他们的工作如何为《平价医疗法案》奠定了基础，该法案是美国历史上最重要、最具争议性的医疗改革之一。

paras.en: We first meet Romney as a young upstart Republican challenger vying to flip Kennedy’s Senate seat in 1994. The race seemed close until a legendary debate. Romney had Kennedy on the defensive until the sitting senator pivoted to the issue near and dear to his heart: health care.
paras.zh: 我们第一次见到罗姆尼是在 1994 年，当时他是一位年轻的新贵共和党挑战者，正在争夺肯尼迪的参议院席位。这场竞选似乎很胶着，直到一场传奇般的辩论。罗姆尼让肯尼迪处于守势，直到现任参议员转向他最关心的问题：医疗保健。

paras.en: “Kennedy is the elder statesman, in command of the issue,” Coss says. “Romney is like an eager student trying to pass the test.” Using his deep knowledge, Kennedy buries the less experienced Romney. In the election, Kennedy then beat Romney by a landslide, even when many Democrats were ousted by Republican challengers that same year. But the loss may have motivated Romney to keep going.
paras.zh: “肯尼迪是年长的政治家，负责解决这个问题，”科斯说。 “罗姆尼就像一个渴望通过考试的学生。”肯尼迪利用他深厚的知识埋葬了经验不足的罗姆尼。在选举中，肯尼迪以压倒性优势击败了罗姆尼，尽管同年许多民主党人被共和党挑战者赶下台。但这次失败可能激励罗姆尼继续前进。

paras.en: Several years later, Romney unexpectedly became a champion of health care reform as the newly elected governor of Massachusetts. The state’s health care system was facing the potential loss of about a billion dollars in federal funding, threatening hospitals that served vulnerable populations. Romney’s administration created Romneycare, which was supported by three features: individual and employer mandates, affordable options for low-income people, and a health care exchange where people could compare plans from different providers.
paras.zh: 几年后，罗姆尼出人意料地成为医疗改革的倡导者，成为新当选的马萨诸塞州州长。该州的医疗保健系统可能面临约 10 亿美元联邦资金的损失，威胁到为弱势群体提供服务的医院。罗姆尼政府创建了罗姆尼医保，它具有三个特点：个人和雇主的强制要求、低收入人群负担得起的选择以及医疗保健交换，人们可以在其中比较不同提供者的计划。

paras.en: With Senator Kennedy’s help, the groundbreaking law passed in 2006 and expanded health insurance coverage to 98 percent of Massachusetts’ population.
paras.zh: 在肯尼迪参议员的帮助下，这项开创性的法律于 2006 年获得通过，将医疗保险覆盖范围扩大到马萨诸塞州 98% 的人口。

paras.en: Romneycare gained national attention and kicked off years-long efforts to replicate it on the federal level. Finally, in 2010, President Obama signed the Affordable Care Act, or ACA. Modeled on Romneycare, the law (colloquially called Obamacare) adapted the reforms made in Massachusetts for all 50 states, a challenge since many states had larger shares of uninsured people than Massachusetts had even before Romneycare.
paras.zh: 罗姆尼医改引起了全国的关注，并开始了长达数年的努力，以在联邦层面复制它。最后，2010 年，奥巴马总统签署了平价医疗法案 (ACA)。该法律（俗称奥巴马医改）以罗姆尼医改为蓝本，将马萨诸塞州的改革适用于所有 50 个州，这是一项挑战，因为许多州没有保险的人口比例甚至比罗姆尼医改之前的马萨诸塞州还要高。

paras.en: The Democrats in Congress also sought to include a government insurance plan in the reform, similar to Medicaid but available to more people. Republicans were wary of the ACA generally, but a government-provided insurance option was a line they wouldn’t cross. The ACA eventually passed without the public option, but by then the political winds had shifted. If there ever was a chance to secure bipartisan support for the law, it was gone by the time Democrats were willing to compromise on the public option. And as soon as the ACA became law, Republicans started fighting it.
paras.zh: 国会民主党人还寻求在改革中纳入政府保险计划，类似于医疗补助计划，但可供更多人使用。共和党人总体上对《平价医疗法案》持谨慎态度，但政府提供的保险选项是他们不会跨越的界限。 《平价医疗法案》最终在没有公众选择的情况下获得通过，但那时政治风向已经发生了转变。如果说曾经有机会获得两党对这项法律的支持，那么当民主党愿意在公众选择上妥协时，这个机会就已经消失了。 《平价医疗法案》一成为法律，共和党人就开始与之抗争。

paras.en: The podcast traces an impressive number of political twists and turns on this health care reform journey. Though I got turned around a few times, I never fully lost the plot thanks to Coss’ well-placed reminders and takeaways.
paras.zh: 该播客追溯了这一医疗改革之旅中令人印象深刻的政治曲折。虽然我被转了好几次，但多亏了科斯的恰到好处的提醒和要点，我从未完全失去了情节。

paras.en: Beyond the story of Romney and Kennedy, the podcast gives voice to many more people who made the ACA a reality: government workers who went from foes to allies who enlisted unlikely help from the conservative Heritage Foundation; longtime friends in the Massachusetts state legislature who were driven apart by the reform; a father who struggled to afford health care and how he advocated for reform with his church. I teared up more than once listening to the human stories behind these policy changes.
paras.zh: 除了罗姆尼和肯尼迪的故事之外，播客还讲述了更多使 ACA 成为现实的人的声音：从敌人变成盟友的政府工作人员，他们从保守的传统基金会那里获得了意想不到的帮助；马萨诸塞州立法机关的老朋友因改革而疏远；一位为支付医疗费用而苦苦挣扎的父亲，以及他如何与教会一起倡导改革。我不止一次在听着这些政策变化背后的人性故事时落泪。

paras.en: Overall, Mitt & Ted gave me new appreciation for why passing a reform is so difficult, despite how life-changing and life-saving access to health care can be. The series points to moments when stars aligned to make reform possible and suggests that more of those opportunities lie ahead.
paras.zh: 总体而言，米特和泰德让我重新认识到为什么通过改革如此困难，尽管获得医疗保健可以改变生活并挽救生命。该系列节目指出了众星齐心协力使改革成为可能的时刻，并表明未来还有更多这样的机会。

paras.en: “The work of American health care remains very much unfinished,” Coss says. “When the perfect alignment of frustration and opportunity arrives again, that might be what determines whether our leaders actually work together.”
paras.zh: “美国医疗保健的工作仍未完成，”科斯说。 “当挫折与机遇完美结合时，这可能决定我们的领导人是否真正合作。”

articles.title: The notion of ‘positive masculinity’ is dividing the male studies field
articles.author: Sujata Gupta

paras.en: Ryon McDermott set out seven years ago to create a new scale measuring masculinity. McDermott, along with other researchers studying male psyches, was tired of the field’s long-standing assertion that the manlier the man, the worse his outcomes. It was high time to measure masculinity in a positive light.
paras.zh: 瑞昂·麦克德莫特七年前开始着手创建一种新的衡量男性气质的量表。麦克德莫特和其他研究男性心理的研究人员厌倦了该领域长期以来的主张，即男人越有男子气概，他的结果就越糟糕。是时候从积极的角度来衡量男性气质了。

paras.en: For almost half a century, the many social science scales that measure gender or masculinity have consistently shown that rigid fealty to Western masculine norms — such as prioritizing work, power-seeking and status — link with poor mental and physical health. Endorsement of such norms also correlates with misogynistic beliefs and violent behaviors, including sexual violence, studies have shown.
paras.zh: 近半个世纪以来，许多衡量性别或男性气质的社会科学量表一致表明，对西方男性规范的严格忠诚——例如优先考虑工作、追求权力和地位——与不良的心理和身体健康有关。研究表明，对此类规范的认可也与厌恶女性的信念和暴力行为（包括性暴力）相关。

paras.en: But giving men a talking-to about their many defects rarely lands well. Nor does that negative focus help men thrive. But what approach would help? “We don’t really have a definition of men’s health. If we don’t know what we are going towards, how can we even do this [research]?” says Matt Englar-Carlson, a counseling expert at California State University, Fullerton.
paras.zh: 但与男人谈论他们的许多缺陷很少能取得好的效果。这种消极的关注也无助于男性的成长。但什么方法会有帮助呢？ “我们对男性健康并没有真正的定义。如果我们不知道我们的目标是什么，我们怎么能进行这项[研究]呢？”加州州立大学富勒顿分校的咨询专家马特·恩格拉尔-卡尔森说。

paras.en: What traits, the researchers wondered, define a healthy man? And could a healthy reframing of manhood improve men’s outcomes, such as by getting them to the doctor or lowering their high rates of social isolation, depression and even death by suicide?
paras.zh: 研究人员想知道什么特征可以定义一个健康的男人？健康地重塑男子气概是否可以改善男性的健康状况，例如让他们去看医生或降低他们的高社会孤立率、抑郁症甚至自杀死亡率？

paras.en: Those questions would cleave the field, though as fights go, this one has been downright nice. McDermott, a psychologist of masculinity at the University of South Alabama in Mobile, would ultimately question positive masculinity’s very existence. Meanwhile, his friends and collaborators at Movember — a nonprofit research organization based in Richmond, Australia that encourages mustache-growing in November to spark conversations around men’s health issues — are poised for a 2027 launch of the Healthy Manhood Index. That scale uses a positive framing and is designed to gauge men’s strengths, while illuminating areas for improvement.
paras.zh: 这些问题将会分裂这个领域，尽管随着战斗的进行，这一场比赛已经非常精彩了。麦克德莫特是南阿拉巴马大学莫比尔分校的男性气质心理学家，他最终质疑积极男性气质的存在。与此同时，他在 Movember 的朋友和合作者准备在 2027 年推出健康男子气概指数。 Movember 是一家位于澳大利亚里士满的非营利性研究组织，鼓励人们在 11 月留胡子，以引发围绕男性健康问题的对话。该量表采用积极的框架，旨在衡量男性的优势，同时指出需要改进的领域。

paras.en: Masculinity is treated as a barrier to health
paras.zh: 男性气质被视为健康的障碍

paras.en: The first gender measurement scale emerged almost a century ago. It positioned femininity and masculinity at opposite poles, with researchers assuming that the most gender-conforming men and women were the healthiest.
paras.zh: 第一个性别测量量表出现于近一个世纪前。它将女性气质和男性气质置于相反的两极，研究人员认为最符合性别的男性和女性是最健康的。

paras.en: That thinking has since unraveled. As women began smashing gender barriers, by doing everything from donning pants to entering the workforce, penalties for women acting more masculine largely disappeared.
paras.zh: 这种想法后来被瓦解了。随着女性开始打破性别障碍，从穿裤子到进入劳动力市场，对表现得更男性化的女性的惩罚基本上消失了。

paras.en: Inspired by the feminist movement, researchers began studying the masculine psyche. Yet they largely framed masculinity as a barrier to health. The Male Role Norms Inventory, one of the most popular masculinity scales in use today, exemplifies that focus. Individuals rank statements like: “A man must stand on his own two feet and never depend on other people to help him do things.”
paras.zh: 受到女权主义运动的启发，研究人员开始研究男性心理。然而，他们在很大程度上将男性气质视为健康的障碍。男性角色规范清单是当今最流行的男性气概量表之一，它体现了这一重点。人们常说：“一个人必须靠自己的两只脚站起来，永远不要依赖别人帮助他做事。”

paras.en: The higher the score on that and more than 60 similar statements appearing in popular masculinity scales used over the past 50 or so years, the worse men’s outcomes, McDermott and his colleagues at Movember reported in July in Men and Masculinities. “Manlier” men often struggle with depression and substance use and engage in sexual aggression. They also tend to avoid asking for help or taking precautionary health measures, such as wearing a mask during the COVID-19 pandemic.
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特和他在 Movember 的同事 7 月在《男性与男性气概》杂志上报告称，在过去 50 多年使用的流行男性气概量表中，得分越高，男性的结果就越差。 “有男子气概”的男人经常与抑郁症和药物滥用作斗争，并进行性侵犯。他们还倾向于避免寻求帮助或采取预防性健康措施，例如在 COVID-19 大流行期间戴口罩。

paras.en: But almost 80 percent of the statements used frame masculinity as a problem to be solved, the team found. That deficit lens biases the findings, argues coauthor and social psychologist Peter Fisher of the Movember Institute of Men’s Health, the organization’s research arm. “If the only tools you have available to you are looking for deficits, you will find deficits,” says Fisher, who is based in Santa Monica, Calif.
paras.zh: 但研究小组发现，近 80% 的陈述将框架男性气概视为需要解决的问题。该组织研究机构莫维贝尔男性健康研究所的合著者、社会心理学家彼得·费舍尔认为，这种缺陷视角会导致研究结果产生偏差。 “如果你可用的唯一工具就是寻找赤字，你就会发现赤字，”住在加利福尼亚州圣莫尼卡的费舍尔说。

paras.en: Researchers pivot to studying positive masculinity
paras.zh: 研究人员转向研究积极的男性气质

paras.en: That negative framing has also seeped into public discourse, so much so that some people now intuitively link “masculinity” with the word “toxic.”
paras.zh: 这种负面框架也渗透到了公共话语中，以至于一些人现在直觉地将“男子气概”与“有毒”一词联系起来。

paras.en: Yet those most macho of men are the outliers, the small percentage who score highest on masculinity scales, Englar-Carlson says. He suspects that what really matters for health is flexibility around when to behave in certain ways. Stoicism, a typically masculine-coded trait, can be calming in emergencies but scary when a man experiences a mental health crisis and refuses help.
paras.zh: 然而，恩格拉-卡尔森说，那些最具男子气概的男性却是异类，即在男子气概量表上得分最高的一小部分人。他怀疑对健康真正重要的是何时以某种方式行事的灵活性。斯多葛主义是一种典型的男性特征，在紧急情况下可以让人平静，但当一个男人经历心理健康危机并拒绝帮助时，它就会令人恐惧。

paras.en: Englar-Carlson and psychologist Mark Kiselica, of Penn State University, Harrisburg, developed the Positive Psychology Positive Masculinity, or PPPM, paradigm in 2010. Public health experts, therapists and others should focus on men’s strengths not deficits, they argued.
paras.zh: 恩格拉尔-卡尔森和哈里斯堡宾夕法尼亚州立大学的心理学家马克·基塞利卡于 2010 年开发了积极心理学积极男子气概（PPPM）范式。他们认为，公共卫生专家、治疗师和其他人应该关注男性的优势而不是缺陷。

paras.en: The ideas in PPPM are what McDermott began trying to turn into a masculinity scale a few years later. But his efforts sent him into a tailspin.
paras.zh: 几年后，麦克德莫特开始尝试将 PPPM 中的想法转化为男性气质量表。但他的努力却让他陷入了困境。

paras.en: He and his colleagues began by identifying positive traits that people linked more with men than women. The team generated a list of 79 possible positive male attributes based on findings from focus groups and studies of positive masculinity and positive psychology, such as “having a good sense of humor,” “serving country or community” and “having passion for one’s work.” More than 1,000 individuals then rated those attributes on a scale from 1 for “strongly disagree” to 7 for “strongly agree” along three dimensions: positive, typically expected of men and typically expected of women.
paras.zh: 他和他的同事首先确定了人们更容易与男性而非女性联系在一起的积极特征。该团队根据焦点小组的调查结果以及积极男子气概和积极心理学的研究，列出了 79 种可能的积极男性特质，例如“有良好的幽默感”、“为国家或社区服务”和“对自己的工作充满热情”。然后，超过 1,000 人根据三个维度对这些属性进行评分，从 1（“强烈不同意”）到 7（“强烈同意”）：积极、通常对男性的期望和通常对女性的期望。

paras.en: Roughly 40 percent of the attributes, particularly those pertaining to protective behaviors and assertiveness, were seen as both positive and expected more of men than of women, McDermott and his colleagues reported in 2019 in Psychology of Men & Masculinities.
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特和他的同事在 2019 年《男性与男性气质心理学》中报告称，大约 40% 的特质，特别是那些与保护行为和自信相关的特质，被认为是男性比女性更积极且更值得期待的特质。

paras.en: But the study also showed that both men and women scored above the midpoint on almost all the allegedly male attributes. That could mean the supposedly gendered attributes had little to do with gender. And for many measures, such as patience and having good hygiene, women scored higher than men. Could that mean that the study’s list was rebranding attributes from feminism as masculine? The idea didn’t sit well with McDermott.
paras.zh: 但研究还表明，男性和女性在几乎所有所谓的男性属性上得分都高于中点。这可能意味着所谓的性别属性与性别几乎没有关系。在许多指标上，例如耐心和良好的卫生习惯，女性的得分高于男性。这是否意味着该研究的清单将女权主义的属性重新标记为男性特征？麦克德莫特并不认同这个想法。

paras.en: Then, the team’s research took a dark turn. The researchers had respondents fill out both their new masculinity survey and a scale measuring sexist beliefs. That revealed that the more strongly respondents endorsed masculine ideals, the more likely they were to endorse sexist beliefs, the team’s unpublished work shows. Think about a statement like, “A good man should be strong,” McDermott says. For many people, that translates to “a good woman should be weak.”
paras.zh: 然后，团队的研究出现了黑暗的转折。研究人员让受访者填写新的男性气质调查和衡量性别歧视信念的量表。该团队未发表的研究表明，这表明受访者越强烈地支持男性理想，他们就越有可能支持性别歧视信仰。想想这样一句话：“一个好人应该坚强，”麦克德莫特说。对于很多人来说，这意味着“好女人应该是软弱的”。

paras.en: “I’ve looked at this across three different samples [of people], and I find the same results each time,” McDermott says. “Whenever you define masculinity, you are inherently defining it against femininity.”
paras.zh: “我对三个不同的[人]样本进行了研究，每次都发现相同的结果，”麦克德莫特说。 “每当你定义男性气质时，你本质上就是在针对女性气质来定义它。”

paras.en: Most attributes are neither male nor female, but human, McDermott has come to believe. And gendering those universal traits merely reinforces sexist stereotypes. The work has left him gutted. “I really thought that there was such thing as positive masculinity,” he says. “But now I believe that it can never truly be positive.”
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特开始相信，大多数属性既不是男性也不是女性，而是人类。而对这些普遍特征进行性别化只会强化性别歧视的刻板印象。这项工作让他心灰意冷。 “我真的认为存在积极的男子气概，”他说。 “但现在我相信它永远不可能真正是积极的。”

paras.en: Fisher is well aware of McDermott’s journey. “He’s been trying to create a positive masculinity scale, or isolate the positive characteristics of masculinity, for a while,” Fisher says. “And he’s been struggling.”
paras.zh: 费舍尔非常了解麦克德莫特的旅程。 “一段时间以来，他一直在尝试创建一个积极的男性气概量表，或者孤立男性气概的积极特征，”费舍尔说。 “而且他一直在挣扎。”

paras.en: Perhaps McDermott has set too high a bar, Fisher says. Rather than trying to identify and measure masculinity through beliefs, he says, why not focus on men’s actions?
paras.zh: 费舍尔说，也许麦克德莫特设定的标准太高了。他说，与其试图通过信仰来识别和衡量男性气质，为什么不关注男性的行为呢？

paras.en: So for the past several years, Fisher and colleagues have been doing just that. They have organized numerous focus groups and tested survey statements with some 12,000 individuals across six countries. Besides addressing the lack of age and cultural diversity used to create most masculinity scales currently in use, Fisher and his team hope that their scale will provide men with a blueprint for what constitutes healthy behavior.
paras.zh: 所以在过去的几年里，费舍尔和他的同事一直在这样做。他们组织了许多焦点小组，并对来自六个国家的约 12,000 人的调查陈述进行了测试。除了解决目前使用的大多数男性气质量表缺乏年龄和文化多样性的问题外，费舍尔和他的团队希望他们的量表能为男性提供健康行为的蓝图。

paras.en: Here’s what a healthy masculinity index might measure
paras.zh: 以下是健康男性气质指数的衡量标准

paras.en: Below are qualities Movember Institute of Men’s Health researchers are evaluating to develop a new masculinity scale. The items are preliminary and may not appear in the final version. The rows show counterproductive behaviors that result from pressures facing men, healthy responses and possible wording for survey statements the men would then rate.
paras.zh: Movember 男性健康研究所的研究人员正在评估以下品质，以开发新的男性气质量表。这些项目是初步的，可能不会出现在最终版本中。这些争吵显示出适得其反的行为，这些行为是由男性面临的压力、健康的反应以及男性随后评分的调查陈述的可能措辞造成的。

paras.en: All the statements in the Healthy Manhood Index start with “I” plus a verb, such as “I do,” “I talk” or “I check in,” Fisher says. For instance, men often feel pressure to restrict their emotions, so the healthy response would be for men to open up emotionally. The index might have men rate a statement like: “I share difficult things I’m going through with people I trust.” Crucially, the higher the score on the index, the healthier the man.
paras.zh: 费舍尔说，健康男子气概指数中的所有陈述都以“我”加动词开头，例如“我做”、“我说话”或“我签到”。例如，男性经常感到有压力去限制自己的情绪，因此健康的反应是男性在情感上敞开心扉。该指数可能会让男性对这样的陈述进行评分：“我与我信任的人分享我正在经历的困难事情。”至关重要的是，该指数得分越高，男人就越健康。

paras.en: Fisher’s goal is to move men toward healthy behaviors without alienating them. “We just want to meet men where they are,” he says.
paras.zh: 费舍尔的目标是在不疏远男性的情况下引导他们采取健康的行为。 “我们只是想在人们所在的地方认识他们，”他说。

paras.en: Should researchers keep or toss masculinity?
paras.zh: 研究人员应该保留还是放弃男性气质？

paras.en: A debate that could easily become acrimonious has remained almost cloyingly friendly. McDermott refers to Fisher as “brilliant.” Fisher credits McDermott for “letting the data change his mind.”
paras.zh: 一场很容易变得激烈的辩论却保持着近乎令人厌烦的友好。麦克德莫特称费舍尔“才华横溢”。费舍尔称赞麦克德莫特“让数据改变了他的想法”。

paras.en: Researchers in the field recognize that they share the same goals, says psychological researcher Michael Addis of Clark University in Worcester, Mass. They want men to be healthier and to treat others, including women and seemingly less masculine men, with respect. “The question is how do we do that? We either sell them on a new masculinity, or we say ‘…. masculinity is always going to be in some ways a box,’” he says.
paras.zh: 马萨诸塞州伍斯特克拉克大学的心理学研究员迈克尔·阿迪斯表示，该领域的研究人员认识到他们有着相同的目标。他们希望男性更健康，并尊重他人，包括女性和看似不那么阳刚的男性。 “问题是我们该如何做到这一点？我们要么向他们推销一种新的男子气概，要么我们说‘……男子气概在某些方面永远是一个盒子，’”他说。

paras.en: Though discussions around how to frame masculinity can feel wonky, the stakes are real, Addis and psychiatrist and behavioral scientist Ethan Hoffmann of Stanford University wrote in 2024 in Psychology of Men & Masculinities.
paras.zh: 艾迪斯和斯坦福大学的精神病学家和行为科学家伊桑·霍夫曼 (Ethan Hoffmann) 在 2024 年的《男性与男性气质心理学》中写道，尽管围绕如何构建男性气质的讨论可能会让人感觉不太靠谱，但其中的利害关系却是真实存在的。

paras.en: Consider suicide. Men who strongly endorsed masculine norms were less likely than others to seek help for depression and more likely to die by suicide, researchers reported in 2025 in Psychiatry International.
paras.zh: 考虑自杀。研究人员于 2025 年在《国际精神病学》杂志上报告称，强烈支持男性规范的男性比其他人更不可能寻求抑郁症帮助，而且更有可能自杀身亡。

paras.en: Theoretically, public health campaigns aimed at men can help. But what form should they take? A positive masculinity campaign may recast a statement like, “real men never ask for help” to “real men know when it’s time to ask for help,” Addis and Hoffman write. But a campaign that rejects gender labels may roll out statements like: “Real men aren’t real: It’s a fiction that could cost you your life.”
paras.zh: 从理论上讲，针对男性的公共卫生运动可以有所帮助。但它们应该采取什么形式呢？阿迪斯和霍夫曼写道，一场积极的男子气概运动可能会将“真正的男人从不寻求帮助”这样的说法改写为“真正的男人知道什么时候该寻求帮助”。但拒绝性别标签的运动可能会推出这样的声明：“真正的男人并不真实：这是一个可能会让你丧命的虚构故事。”

paras.en: Such postgender messaging may feel too abstract for the average guy, Fisher says. Convincing a 65-year-old man to stay on top of his prostate cancer appointments is hard enough without trying to shift his worldview.
paras.zh: 费舍尔说，这种后性别信息对于普通人来说可能感觉太抽象了。如果不试图改变一名 65 岁的男性的世界观，说服他继续做好前列腺癌的预约就已经够困难的了。

paras.en: McDermott counters that positive masculinity “makes the sex role stuff continue,” enshrining the idea that gender roles and hierarchies constitute a necessary organizing principle for societies.
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特反驳说，积极的男子气概“让性别角色的东西继续存在”，并坚信性别角色和等级制度构成了社会必要的组织原则。

paras.en: Reconciliation may be possible, Addis says. Policy makers and public health experts could first rope men in with a more positive masculine approach. Then over time, they could help men question and relinquish gender norms. “I call it dancing with the devil,” or temporarily adopting the gendered approach as a means to a desired end, he says.
paras.zh: 阿迪斯说，和解是可能的。政策制定者和公共卫生专家可以首先以更积极的男性方式吸引男性参与。然后随着时间的推移，它们可以帮助男性质疑并放弃性别规范。他说，“我称之为与魔鬼共舞”，或者暂时采用性别化的方式作为达到预期目的的手段。

paras.en: However the debate unfurls, researchers are writing their own script on how to fight like real men — or real people. “There’s a lot of men in the psychology of men [field] who have worked really hard to not let our egos get in the way of good work,” Addis says. “It’s sort of like practice what you preach.”
paras.zh: 无论争论如何展开，研究人员正在编写自己的脚本，讲述如何像真正的男人或真人一样战斗。 “在男性心理学领域，有很多男性非常努力地工作，不让我们的自负妨碍我们做好工作，”阿迪斯说。 “这有点像言行一致。”

paras.en: If you or someone you care about may be at risk of suicide, the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline offers free, 24/7 support, information and local resources from trained counselors. Call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org.
paras.zh: 如果您或您关心的人可能有自杀风险，988 自杀和危机生命热线可提供来自训练有素的咨询师的免费 24/7 支持、信息和本地资源。致电或发短信 988 或通过 988lifeline.org 聊天。

articles.title: Popular Skincare Ingredient Lowers Inflammation Markers in 12-Week Clinical Trial
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: They say beauty is only skin deep, but a common skincare ingredient appears to have effects that extend much further than that.
