articles.title: NMG Gives UAC, Precision Vendor of the Year Awards
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: NexaMotion Group (NMG) named UAC (Universal Air Conditioner, Inc.) and Precision International the recipients of its first annual Vendor of the Year award.
paras.zh: NexaMotion Group (NMG) 将 UAC (Universal Air Conditioner, Inc.) 和 Precision International 授予其首个年度供应商奖。

paras.en: According to NMG, honorees were selected by NMG’s executive and supply chain leadership on “availability, quality and responsiveness, and on a harder test: how far the supplier was willing to go in service of NMG’s strategy and its customers’ success.”
paras.zh: 据 NMG 称，获奖者是由 NMG 的高管和供应链领导层根据“可用性、质量和响应能力，以及更严格的测试：供应商愿意在多大程度上为 NMG 的战略和客户的成功服务”而选出的。

paras.en: “Anyone can fill an order. Our best partners help us build the business,” said Scott Weinstein, president of NexaMotion Group. “UAC and Precision International show up in the planning room, not just on the loading dock. They bring us coverage before our customers ask for it, they invest in our people and our shops, and when we make bold moves as a company they are right beside us. That is partnership, and it is what this award was created to honor.”
paras.zh: “任何人都可以填写订单。我们最好的合作伙伴帮助我们发展业务，”NexaMotion Group 总裁 Scott Weinstein 说道。 “UAC 和 Precision International 出现在规划室，而不仅仅是装货码头。他们在客户提出要求之前就为我们提供报道，他们对我们的员工和商店进行投资，当我们作为一家公司采取大胆行动时，他们就在我们身边。这就是合作伙伴关系，这也是这个奖项的设立的目的。”

articles.title: BendPak Releases OctaFlex Series Lifts
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: BendPak Inc. released the OctaFlex Series of eight-arm car lifts. The OctaFlex12DPS two-post lift is now shipping.
paras.zh: BendPak Inc. 发布了 OctaFlex 系列八臂汽车举升机。 OctaFlex12DPS 两柱移位机现已发货。

paras.en: According to the company, this is how it works: “While the four primary arms support the vehicle, the four secondary arms can raise, lower or simply hold cabs, drivetrains, EV batteries, suspension assemblies and other heavy components without the need for additional equipment, helpers or bays. When they’re not required, the auxiliary arms can be moved up out of the way, so the lift can be used as a standard two-post model.”
paras.zh: 据该公司介绍，它的工作原理是这样的：“四个主臂支撑车辆，四个辅助臂可以升高、降低或简单地支撑驾驶室、传动系统、电动汽车电池、悬架总成和其他重型部件，而无需额外的设备、助手或托架。当不需要时，辅助臂可以向上移开，因此升降机可以用作标准的两柱模型。”

paras.en: It also comes with a magnetic pendant controller with two-speed controls. The pendant controller lets technicians stand back from the lift columns for enhanced visibility around the vehicle. Each set of arms can be operated independently at either “normal” or new “slow” speed.
paras.zh: 它还配备了具有两种速度控制的磁性吊坠控制器。悬吊式控制器让技术人员可以站在升降柱后面，以增强车辆周围的视野。每组手臂都可以以“正常”或新的“慢速”速度独立操作。

paras.en: “As dealers and independent repair shops continue to struggle with an aging and shrinking technician workforce, they also face surging demand for labor-intensive tasks like cab-off repairs and EV service,” says Jeff Kritzer, BendPak president and CEO. “OctaFlex eases the pressure by helping technicians handle complex jobs independently with greater efficiency and less physical strain, maximizing throughput and profit potential.”
paras.zh: BendPak 总裁兼首席执行官杰夫·克里泽 (Jeff Kritzer) 表示：“随着经销商和独立维修店继续应对技术人员队伍老化和萎缩的问题，他们还面临着出租车维修和电动汽车服务等劳动密集型任务的需求激增。” “OctaFlex 通过帮助技术人员以更高的效率和更少的体力独立处理复杂的工作来减轻压力，从而最大限度地提高吞吐量和利润潜力。”

articles.title: Alliance Big Kahuna Sweepstakes Nearing End
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: The Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Inc. announced that its fall Big Kahuna Getaway Sweepstakes is nearing an end, with a week left until the Nov. 30 deadline to win a trip to Hawaii.
paras.zh: 售后汽车配件联盟 (Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Inc.) 宣布，其秋季 Big Kahuna Getaway 抽奖活动即将结束，距离赢得夏威夷之旅的最后期限 11 月 30 日还有一周时间。

paras.en: The promotion gives technicians the opportunity to participate through MyPlace4Parts by earning entries with qualifying purchases for a chance to win one of 25 trips for two to Oahu or a share of $45,000 in gift card prizes.
paras.zh: 此次促销活动让技术人员有机会通过 MyPlace4Parts 参与活动，通过符合条件的购买获得参赛资格，有机会赢得 25 次前往欧胡岛的两人旅行中的一次，或者分享 45,000 美元的礼品卡奖品。

paras.en: In May 2027, winners and their guests will enjoy six nights and seven days in Oahu, including accommodations, travel, exclusive meals and receptions, VIP experiences, and curated activities.
paras.zh: 2027 年 5 月，获奖者及其宾客将在欧胡岛享受 7 天 6 晚的住宿，包括住宿、旅行、专属餐食和招待会、VIP 体验和策划活动。

paras.en: “We want to thank every technician and shop participating in the Big Kahuna Getaway and helping make this promotion such an exciting opportunity,” said Kendall Lozano, sales and marketing manager for the Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Inc. “We know how hard our customers work every day, and we’re excited to have the opportunity to give them something to look forward to. We also want to extend our sincere thanks to our channel partners whose continued support helps make experiences like this possible. We’re looking forward to celebrating with our winners and welcoming them to Oahu next May.”
paras.zh: 售后汽车零部件联盟公司销售和营销经理 Kendall Lozano 表示：“我们要感谢参与 Big Kahuna Getaway 的每一位技术人员和商店，他们帮助使这次促销活动成为一个令人兴奋的机会。我们知道我们的客户每天工作有多么辛苦，我们很高兴有机会为他们提供一些值得期待的东西。我们还要向我们的渠道合作伙伴表示诚挚的谢意，他们的持续支持使这样的体验成为可能。我们期待与获奖者一起庆祝，并欢迎明年五月他们将前往欧胡岛。”

articles.title: NMG Gives UAC, Precision Vendor of the Year Awards

articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: The Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Inc. announced that its fall Big Kahuna Getaway Sweepstakes is nearing an end, with a week left until the Nov. 30 deadline to win a trip to Hawaii.
paras.zh: 售后汽车配件联盟 (Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Inc.) 宣布，其秋季 Big Kahuna Getaway 抽奖活动即将结束，距离赢得夏威夷之旅的最后期限 11 月 30 日还有一周时间。

paras.en: The promotion gives technicians the opportunity to participate through MyPlace4Parts by earning entries with qualifying purchases for a chance to win one of 25 trips for two to Oahu or a share of $45,000 in gift card prizes.
paras.zh: 此次促销活动让技术人员有机会通过 MyPlace4Parts 参与活动，通过符合条件的购买获得参赛资格，有机会赢得 25 次前往欧胡岛的两人旅行中的一次，或者分享 45,000 美元的礼品卡奖品。

paras.en: In May 2027, winners and their guests will enjoy six nights and seven days in Oahu, including accommodations, travel, exclusive meals and receptions, VIP experiences, and curated activities.
paras.zh: 2027 年 5 月，获奖者及其宾客将在欧胡岛享受 7 天 6 晚的住宿，包括住宿、旅行、专属餐食和招待会、VIP 体验和策划活动。

paras.en: “We want to thank every technician and shop participating in the Big Kahuna Getaway and helping make this promotion such an exciting opportunity,” said Kendall Lozano, sales and marketing manager for the Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Inc. “We know how hard our customers work every day, and we’re excited to have the opportunity to give them something to look forward to. We also want to extend our sincere thanks to our channel partners whose continued support helps make experiences like this possible. We’re looking forward to celebrating with our winners and welcoming them to Oahu next May.”
paras.zh: 售后汽车零部件联盟公司销售和营销经理 Kendall Lozano 表示：“我们要感谢参与 Big Kahuna Getaway 的每一位技术人员和商店，他们帮助使这次促销活动成为一个令人兴奋的机会。我们知道我们的客户每天工作有多么辛苦，我们很高兴有机会为他们提供一些值得期待的东西。我们还要向我们的渠道合作伙伴表示诚挚的谢意，他们的持续支持使这样的体验成为可能。我们期待与获奖者一起庆祝，并欢迎明年五月他们将前往欧胡岛。”

articles.title: NABC, Partners Donate Recycled Ride to Navy Veteran
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: On Tuesday, Nov. 17, a U.S. Navy veteran and single mother from the Twin Cities received a refurbished vehicle to help her maintain employment, continue building a sustainable future and create greater opportunities for herself and her family. The donation was made possible by the NABC Recycled Rides program, vehicle donor Farmers and repair partner Heppner’s Auto Body & Glass.
paras.zh: 11 月 17 日星期二，一位来自双城的美国海军退伍军人和单身母亲收到了一辆翻新车辆，以帮助她维持就业、继续建设可持续的未来并为自己和家人创造更多机会。此次捐赠是由 NABC Recycled Rides 计划、车辆捐赠者 Farmers 和维修合作伙伴 Heppner’s Auto Body & Glass 共同促成的。

paras.en: The recipient was nominated by the Minnesota Assistance Council for Veterans, whose mission is to end veteran homelessness in Minnesota.
paras.zh: 获奖者是由明尼苏达州退伍军人援助委员会提名的，该委员会的使命是结束明尼苏达州退伍军人无家可归的现象。

paras.en: Stacya May is a U.S. Navy veteran who proudly served from 2012 to 2017, conducting mine countermeasures. During her military service, she deployed to Bahrain in June 2014 and earned her Air Warfare pin. She was honorably discharged after five years of service.
paras.zh: 斯塔西娅·梅 (Stacya May) 是一名美国海军退伍军人，曾在 2012 年至 2017 年期间服役，从事反水雷工作。在服兵役期间，她于 2014 年 6 月被部署到巴林并获得了空战徽章。服役五年后，她光荣退役。

paras.en: Today, May is focused on building a stable and successful future for her and her family. She is currently attending college, pursuing a degree in supply chain logistics. Her goal is to complete her two-year degree and transfer to the University of Minnesota to continue her education.
paras.zh: 如今，梅专注于为她和她的家人打造稳定和成功的未来。她目前正在上大学，攻读供应链物流学位。她的目标是完成两年制学位并转学到明尼苏达大学继续学业。

paras.en: This vehicle will allow her to transport her disabled cousin to medical appointments, provide safer and more dependable transportation for her child, help maintain her educational commitments and support the stability that she has worked hard to achieve.
paras.zh: 这辆车将使她能够运送她残疾的表弟去就医，为她的孩子提供更安全、更可靠的交通，帮助维持她的教育承诺，并支持她努力实现的稳定。

paras.en: Additional partners in this presentation included: Enterprise; O’Reilly; Finishing Touch Car Care; Roseville Midway Ford; Auto Images; Southeast Towing; Showroom Auto Care; PPG; Inver Grove Honda; Advanced Vehicle Solutions; Advanced Remarketing Services; Cars for Charity; and Copart.
paras.zh: 本次演示中的其他合作伙伴包括：Enterprise；奥莱利；画龙点睛的汽车护理；罗斯维尔中途福特；汽车图像；东南拖车；展厅汽车护理； PPG；因弗格罗夫本田；先进的车辆解决方案；高级再营销服务；慈善汽车；和科帕特。

paras.en: Individuals in the community can support this program in two ways — donate to the program directly or donate their unwanted or non-running vehicle through the Changing and Saving Lives Keys for Change program. They will receive a tax donation for their contribution, and proceeds will help provide reliable transportation for those in need across the country — and in their community.
paras.zh: 社区中的个人可以通过两种方式支持该计划——直接向该计划捐款，或者通过“改变和拯救生命钥匙促进改变”计划捐赠他们不需要或未运行的车辆。他们的贡献将获得税收捐赠，收益将有助于为全国各地及其社区有需要的人提供可靠的交通。

paras.en: Farmers, a level one partner of the NABC, has donated nearly 100 vehicles to people and organizations through the Recycled Rides program.
paras.zh: Farmers 是 NABC 的一级合作伙伴，已通过“回收乘车”计划向个人和组织捐赠了近 100 辆车辆。

paras.en: Heppner’s Auto Body & Glass is an I-CAR Gold Class repair facility. With six locations, they have been serving the Twin Cities for more than 65 years, and have presented multiple Recycled Rides to people in need in their local community.
paras.zh: Heppner 的汽车车身和玻璃是一家 I-CAR 黄金级维修厂。他们拥有六个地点，为双子城提供服务已超过 65 年，并向当地社区有需要的人们提供了多个回收游乐设施。

articles.title: AUMOVIO’s Global Startup Co-pace Accelerates AI Innovation
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: AUMOVIO’s global startup organization co-pace, recently hosted the Automotive AI Startup Innovation Challenge, bringing together 10 startups to explore AI technologies with potential real-world applications. It was hosted at Newlab Detroit.
paras.zh: AUMOVIO的全球创业组织co-pace最近举办了汽车人工智能创业创新挑战赛，汇聚了10家初创公司，共同探索人工智能技术与潜在的实际应用。它在底特律 Newlab 举办。

paras.en: The event was designed to connect startups with AUMOVIO in order to create opportunities to support the next generation of software-defined and AI-enabled vehicles.
paras.zh: 该活动旨在将初创公司与AUMOVIO联系起来，以创造支持下一代软件定义和人工智能车辆的机会。

paras.en: “Innovation and connectivity are intertwined,” said Dr. Otmar Schreiner, managing director of co-pace. “Our startup organization is experienced in connecting AUMOVIO with a global network of startups and exploring new opportunities, together. Expanding these connections in North America allows us to invest in the pursuit of what is next.”
paras.zh: “创新和连通性是交织在一起的，”copace 董事总经理 Otmar Schreiner 博士说。 “我们的初创企业组织在将 AUMOVIO 与全球初创企业网络联系起来并共同探索新机会方面拥有丰富的经验。在北美扩大这些联系使我们能够投资于追求未来。”

paras.en: Through co-pace, the company engages with several hundred startups annually around the world, helping bring innovation closer to the business. This challenge strengthens co-pace’s involvement in North America, welcoming new avenues to connect with external tech ecosystems.
paras.zh: 通过 co-pace，该公司每年与全球数百家初创公司合作，帮助创新更贴近业务。这一挑战加强了 copace 在北美的参与，欢迎与外部技术生态系统建立联系的新途径。

paras.en: Exploration Into the Next Generation of AI
paras.zh: 探索下一代人工智能

paras.en: The challenge focused on four technology areas relevant to AUMOVIO: AI compute platforms, AI orchestration software, intelligent zonal architecture, and fleet learning data platforms. Each addresses critical aspects of intelligent infrastructure needed to support advanced applications. As vehicles become more AI-enabled, the demand for secure, reliable integration throughout the vehicle’s life cycle is imperative, the company said.
paras.zh: 本次挑战赛重点关注与 AUMOVIO 相关的四个技术领域：AI 计算平台、AI 编排软件、智能分区架构和车队学习数据平台。每个解决方案都解决了支持高级应用程序所需的智能基础设施的关键方面。该公司表示，随着车辆越来越多地支持人工智能，在整个车辆生命周期中安全、可靠的集成的需求势在必行。

paras.en: Participating startups presented solutions that were evaluated for technical feasibility, integration capabilities, runtime monitoring, security, and measurable improvements in model performance and data usability. The objective was to identify an approach that could complement AUMOVIO’s existing capabilities while supporting further exploration, validation, and potential integration.
paras.zh: 参与的初创公司提出了解决方案，并对技术可行性、集成能力、运行时监控、安全性以及模型性能和数据可用性的可衡量改进进行了评估。目标是确定一种方法，可以补充 AUMOVIO 的现有功能，同时支持进一步的探索、验证和潜在的集成。

paras.en: A winner will be selected to advance toward a proof of concept (PoC). The next phase is to evaluate the selected technology’s potential application within AUMOVIO’s systems. For AUMOVIO, the collaboration provides an additional pipeline to startup talent, new ideas, and solutions in AI-enabled systems, the company said.
paras.zh: 将选出一名获胜者来推进概念验证 (PoC)。下一阶段是评估所选技术在 AUMOVIO 系统中的潜在应用。该公司表示，对于 AUMOVIO 来说，此次合作为人工智能系统中的初创人才、新想法和解决方案提供了额外的渠道。

paras.en: “Our innovation strategy requires us to anticipate what comes next and learn how to harness it,” shared Seyed Hajimirza, head of innovation, AUMOVIO, North America. “We can challenge conventional approaches and forge new pathways by collaborating with technology partners. That’s how we continue to lead.”
paras.zh: “我们的创新战略要求我们预测接下来会发生什么，并学习如何利用它，”AUMOVIO 北美创新主管 Seyed Hajimirza 分享道。 “我们可以通过与技术合作伙伴合作挑战传统方法并开辟新途径。这就是我们继续保持领先地位的方式。”

articles.title: How Technology Adoption, Duty Cycle Shape Fleet Fuel Economy
articles.author: Kevin Linger

paras.en: Fleet fuel economy improved 18% from 2010 to 2025, according to a North American Council for Freight Efficiency (NACFE) study. Participants averaged 7.48 MPG in 2025. The study results help show why equipment decisions need to reflect the work.
paras.zh: 根据北美货运效率委员会 (NACFE) 的一项研究，从 2010 年到 2025 年，车队燃油经济性提高了 18%。 2025 年，参与者平均每加仑行驶 7.48 英里。研究结果有助于说明为什么设备决策需要反映工作情况。

paras.en: The 2026 Fleet Efficiency Study separated linehaul and regional-haul results for the first time. Linehaul fleets reached a study record of 7.96 MPG, while regional fleets averaged 7.29 MPG.
paras.zh: 2026 年机队效率研究首次将长途运输和支线运输结果分开。长途运输车队的研究记录达到了 7.96 MPG，而支线车队的平均里程为 7.29 MPG。

paras.en: Those numbers provide benchmarks, but routes, payloads, and equipment affect how useful each comparison will be. A fleet moving toward shorter routes can face pressure on its average MPG while continuing to invest in efficiency.
paras.zh: 这些数字提供了基准，但路线、载荷和设备会影响每次比较的实用性。如果车队转向较短的路线，其平均英里油耗可能会面临压力，同时仍需继续在提高效率方面投入资金。

paras.en: The report covers Class 8 tractors and trailers and tracks adoption of more than 80 technologies and practices. Fifteen fleets supplied 2024 and 2025 data for this update. Across the study’s history, 29 fleets contributed data reaching back to 2003.
paras.zh: 本报告涵盖8级牵引车和挂车，并跟踪了80多项技术和做法的采用情况。15 家车队为本次更新提供了 2024 年和 2025 年的数据。在整个研究历史中，有29家车队提供了可追溯至2003年的数据。

paras.en: Regional operations typically involve more stops and more time on local roads than linehaul work. Regional fleets represented 57% of study participants in 2025, compared with 35% in 2010, influencing the combined results.
paras.zh: 与干线运输相比，区域运营通常涉及更多的停靠点和更长的本地道路行驶时间。2025年，区域车队占研究参与者的57%，而2010年为35%，这影响了综合结果。

paras.en: During the report’s press conference, Mike Roeth, NACFE’s executive director, raised a familiar specification problem. One tractor may perform highway work overnight and local deliveries during the day, complicating choices about gearing, aerodynamics, and idle reduction.
paras.zh: During the report’s press conference, Mike Roeth, NACFE’s executive director, raised a familiar specification problem.一台拖拉机可能在夜间执行高速公路作业，并在白天执行本地交付，这使得有关传动装置、空气动力学和怠速减少的选择变得复杂。

paras.en: “Now, when you get into some LTL operations where you’ve got both a long distance, say nighttime run, and then that same truck’s used in the city during the day, that becomes an interesting and challenging spec challenge,” Roeth said.
paras.zh: “现在，当你进入一些零担运输业务时，你既要进行长距离（比如夜间运行），又要在白天在城市中使用同一辆卡车，这就成为一个有趣且具有挑战性的规格挑战，”罗思说。

paras.en: The practical question is how much time the truck spends in each part of that operation. Its highway mileage, stops, and idling needs help determine which features can earn their cost.
paras.zh: 实际问题是卡车在该操作的每个部分花费了多少时间。它的高速公路里程、停车和怠速需求有助于确定哪些功能可以赚取成本。

paras.en: Roeth also challenged the assumption that daycabs see too little highway use to benefit from aerodynamic equipment. He said growing recognition of their highway operation is supporting adoption of efficiency technologies.
paras.zh: 罗思还对日间出租车在高速公路上的使用太少而无法从空气动力设备中受益的假设提出了质疑。他说，人们对高速公路运营的日益认可正在支持高效技术的采用。

paras.en: Fleet practices and powertrain technologies were the most widely adopted categories in both duty cycles. Linehaul fleets generally adopted tractor aerodynamics and idle reduction at higher rates, reflecting differences in how the equipment operates.
paras.zh: 车队实践和动力总成技术是两个工作周期中采用最广泛的类别。长途运输车队通常采用拖拉机空气动力学技术并以更高的速率减少怠速，这反映了设备运行方式的差异。

paras.en: Among linehaul fleets, automated manual transmission adoption rose from 22% in 2007 to 86% in 2025. Downspeeding, defined in the report as a final drive ratio below 2.7:1, rose from 13% to 98%.
paras.zh: 在长途运输车队中，手自一体变速箱的采用率从 2007 年的 22% 上升到 2025 年的 86%。降速（报告中定义为最终传动比低于 2.7:1）从 13% 上升到 98%。

paras.en: The study also identified gains in routing optimization and vehicle data analysis for fuel efficiency. These practices give fleets opportunities to improve how they use equipment alongside changes to the truck itself.
paras.zh: 该研究还确定了路线优化和车辆数据分析在燃油效率方面的收益。这些做法为车队提供了改进设备使用方式以及卡车本身的机会。

paras.en: Higher technology adoption correlated with higher MPG, but NACFE cautioned that the relationship does not establish causation. Fleets investing heavily in equipment may also follow other practices contributing to their results.
paras.zh: 更高的技术采用率与更高的 MPG 相关，但 NACFE 警告说，这种关系并不能建立因果关系。大量投资设备的船队也可能会遵循其他有助于其结果的做法。

paras.en: Read the full article on fleetequipmentmag.com.
paras.zh: 请在 fancyequipmentmag.com 上阅读完整文章。

articles.title: AACF Golf Tournament Raises Record $700,000
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: The Automotive Aftermarket Charitable Foundation (AACF) celebrated the success of its 34th annual Bob Schoeberl Memorial Charity Golf Tournament. The event took place Nov. 1-2 at Spanish Trail Country Club in Las Vegas. The sold-out event brought together 216 golfers and other automotive aftermarket industry supporters for two days of networking and competition.
paras.zh: 汽车售后市场慈善基金会 (AACF) 庆祝其第 34 届年度鲍勃·舍伯尔纪念慈善高尔夫锦标赛取得成功。该活动于 11 月 1 日至 2 日在拉斯维加斯西班牙小径乡村俱乐部举行。此次活动门票全部售完，共有 216 名高尔夫球手和其他汽车售后市场行业支持者齐聚一堂，进行为期两天的交流和比赛。

paras.en: Fundraising activities included the tournament, live auction, prize drawings and golf pro experiences. These activities raised nearly $700,000, marking the highest total in the event’s history. The funds will help AACF provide financial assistance to aftermarket families facing unexpected hardships.
paras.zh: 筹款活动包括锦标赛、现场拍卖、抽奖和高尔夫职业体验。这些活动筹集了近 70 万美元，创下了该活动历史上的最高总额。这些资金将帮助 AACF 为面临意外困难的售后家庭提供经济援助。

paras.en: AACF Tournament Supports Aftermarket Families
paras.zh: AACF 锦标赛为售后市场家庭提供支持

paras.en: “When a member of the automotive aftermarket community faces an unexpected hardship, the support of this industry can make all the difference,” said John Kairys, executive director of AACF. “The generosity of everyone who participated in this year’s tournament will help ensure that individuals and families facing some of life’s most difficult moments know they aren’t alone. We’re thankful and appreciative that this community comes together year after year for such an important cause.”
paras.zh: AACF 执行董事 John Kairys 表示：“当汽车售后市场社区的成员面临意想不到的困难时，该行业的支持可以发挥重要作用。” “参加今年比赛的每个人的慷慨将有助于确保面临生活中最困难时刻的个人和家庭知道他们并不孤单。我们感谢和赞赏这个社区年复一年地为了如此重要的事业聚集在一起。”

paras.en: Historic Hole-in-One Highlights Tournament
paras.zh: 历史性一杆进洞精彩赛事

paras.en: Among this year’s tournament highlights, Sean McLoraine became the first participant in the event’s 34-year history to win the hole-in-one contest. Interstate Batteries sponsored the contest, which featured a new 2026 Toyota Tundra as its grand prize.
paras.zh: 在今年赛事的亮点中，肖恩·麦克洛兰 (Sean McLoraine) 成为该赛事 34 年历史上第一位赢得一杆进洞比赛的参赛者。 Interstate Batteries sponsored the contest, which featured a new 2026 Toyota Tundra as its grand prize.

paras.en: “I look forward to this tournament every year because I love seeing our industry come together to give back to the people who make it what it is,” said Jeff Helfrich, AACF golf committee chairman. “To raise a record amount for aftermarket families and have Sean McLoraine make the first hole-in-one for a vehicle in our 34 years of playing this event made this a year I’ll always remember. Congratulations to Sean on his new Toyota Tundra and thank you to Interstate Batteries for sponsoring the contest.”
paras.zh: AACF 高尔夫委员会主席杰夫·赫尔弗里奇 (Jeff Helfrich) 表示：“我每年都期待着这项赛事，因为我喜欢看到我们的行业齐心协力，回馈那些做出今天的贡献的人们。” “为售后家庭筹集了创纪录的金额，并让肖恩·麦克洛兰 (Sean McLoraine) 在我们参加这项赛事 34 年来首次打进一杆进洞，这让我永远铭记这一年。祝贺肖恩 (Sean) 拥有他的新丰田坦途 (Toyota Tundra)，并感谢 Interstate Batteries 对本次比赛的赞助。”

paras.en: AACF thanked the participants, sponsors, donors, volunteers and industry partners who supported this year’s tournament. Those interested in participating in or sponsoring the 2027 Bob Schoeberl Memorial Golf Tournament can click here for updates and additional information.
paras.zh: AACF 感谢支持今年比赛的参赛者、赞助商、捐助者、志愿者和行业合作伙伴。 Those interested in participating in or sponsoring the 2027 Bob Schoeberl Memorial Golf Tournament can click here for updates and additional information.

articles.title: Big Kahuna Getaway Sweepstakes Fall Promotion Wrapping Up
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: The Big Kahuna Getaway Sweepstakes is bringing an exciting fall promotion to a close, giving professional technicians across North America one final opportunity to earn entries, win prizes, and get one step closer to an unforgettable getaway to Oahu, Hawaii.
paras.zh: Big Kahuna Getaway 抽奖活动即将结束，激动人心的秋季促销活动即将结束，为北美各地的专业技术人员提供最后一次机会，赢得参赛资格、赢取奖品，距离夏威夷欧胡岛难忘的度假更近一步。

paras.en: Running from September through November, the promotion gives technicians the opportunity to participate through MyPlace4Parts by earning entries with qualifying purchases for a chance to win one of 25 trips for two to Oahu or a share of $45,000 in gift card prizes. With the promotion wrapping up November 30, there’s still time for eligible participants to get in on the excitement!
paras.zh: 该促销活动从 9 月持续到 11 月，技术人员有机会通过 MyPlace4Parts 参与活动，通过符合资格的购买获得参赛资格，有机会赢得 25 次前往瓦胡岛的两人旅行中的一次，或分享 45,000 美元的礼品卡奖品。促销活动将于 11 月 30 日结束，符合资格的参与者还有时间享受兴奋！

paras.en: The 25 lucky winners will soon have the opportunity to trade their toolboxes for tropical breezes. In May 2027, winners and their guests will enjoy six nights and seven days in Oahu, including accommodations, travel, exclusive meals and receptions, VIP experiences, and curated activities designed to showcase the beauty, culture, and aloha spirit of the island.
paras.zh: 25 名幸运获奖者很快将有机会用他们的工具箱换取热带微风。 2027 年 5 月，获奖者及其宾客将在欧胡岛享受 7 天 6 晚的住宿，包括住宿、旅行、专属餐食和招待会、VIP 体验以及旨在展示该岛美丽、文化和阿罗哈精神的精心策划的活动。

paras.en: “We want to thank every technician and shop participating in The Big Kahuna Getaway and helping make this promotion such an exciting opportunity,” said Kendall Lozano, sales and marketing manager for the Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Inc. “We know how hard our customers work every day, and we’re excited to have the opportunity to give them something to look forward to. We also want to extend our sincere thanks to our channel partners whose continued support helps make experiences like this possible. We’re looking forward to celebrating with our winners and welcoming them to Oahu next May.”
paras.zh: 售后汽车配件联盟公司销售和营销经理 Kendall Lozano 表示：“我们要感谢参加 The Big Kahuna Getaway 的每一位技术人员和商店，他们帮助我们使这次促销活动成为一个令人兴奋的机会。我们知道我们的客户每天工作有多么辛苦，我们很高兴有机会为他们提供一些值得期待的东西。我们还要向我们的渠道合作伙伴表示诚挚的谢意，他们的持续支持使这样的体验成为可能。我们期待与获奖者一起庆祝，并欢迎他们的到来。”明年五月他们将前往欧胡岛。”

paras.en: The Big Kahuna Getaway is powered through MyPlace4Parts, giving participating technicians the opportunity to earn entries while placing their everyday orders. Every qualifying $150 invoice earns one entry, with bonus entries awarded for additional $150 increments purchased throughout the promotion.
paras.zh: The Big Kahuna Getaway is powered through MyPlace4Parts, giving participating technicians the opportunity to earn entries while placing their everyday orders.每一张符合条件的 150 美元发票均可获得一次参与机会，在整个促销活动期间购买额外 150 美元的增量即可获得奖励参与机会。

paras.en: As the final days of the sweepstakes approach, anticipation continues to build for the 25 winners who will soon be on their way to Waikiki for an unforgettable island experience filled with adventure, relaxation, and plenty of aloha.
paras.zh: 随着抽奖活动最后几天的临近，人们对 25 名获奖者的期待不断增强，他们很快将前往威基基，享受充满冒险、放松和阿罗哈风情的难忘岛屿体验。

paras.en: “Promotions like The Big Kahuna Getaway are made possible through the incredible support of our customers, our channel partners, and the entire Auto Value and Bumper to Bumper network,” added Lozano. “We’re grateful to everyone participating and helping bring this promotion to life. We can’t wait to celebrate our winners and give them an experience they’ll remember for years to come. There’s still time to enter, and we look forward to seeing everyone in Oahu!”
paras.zh: “像 Big Kahuna Getaway 这样的促销活动是通过我们的客户、渠道合作伙伴以及整个 Auto Value 和 Bumper to Bumper 网络的大力支持才得以实现的，”Lozano 补充道。 “我们感谢所有参与并帮助实现这一促销活动的人。我们迫不及待地想要庆祝我们的获奖者，并为他们提供一次终生难忘的体验。还有时间参加，我们期待在欧胡岛见到大家！”

articles.title: It's time to look at Uranus: How to see the solar system's strangest planet at its best this week
articles.author: Jamie Carter

paras.en: One of the hardest planets to see in the solar system — the distant ice giant Uranus — reaches its annual opposition on Wednesday (Nov. 25), just a day after the Beaver Supermoon. It's the best time to see the seventh planet from the sun, but you'll need to use stargazing binoculars or a good backyard telescope to find it.
paras.zh: 太阳系中最难观测到的行星之一——遥远的冰巨星天王星——将于周三（11 月 25 日）到达一年一度的冲日点，就在海狸超级月亮发生的第二天。这是观看太阳第七颗行星的最佳时间，但您需要使用观星双筒望远镜或良好的后院望远镜才能找到它。

paras.en: Uranus is faint, slow-moving and rarely a target for casual stargazers. However, on Nov. 25, and, for a few weeks on either side, it will be at its closest point to Earth this year and will appear at its brightest, making it possible to spot.
paras.zh: 天王星亮度微弱，移动缓慢，很少成为休闲观星者的目标。然而，在 11 月 25 日，以及两侧的几周内，它将位于今年距离地球最近的位置，并且将出现在最亮的位置，从而使观测成为可能。

paras.en: Opposition occurs when Earth passes between Uranus and the sun; Uranus will be "opposite" the sun, hence, "opposition." The moment of opposition will happen at 6 p.m. ET on Nov. 25, according to EarthSky. Consequently, Uranus will rise in the east around sunset, reach its highest point in the sky around midnight and set in the west around sunrise.
paras.zh: 当地球经过天王星和太阳之间时，就会发生冲分。天王星将与太阳“对冲”，因此是“对冲”。反对的时刻将在下午 6 点发生。据 EarthSky 报道，美国东部时间 11 月 25 日。因此，天王星将在日落时分从东方升起，在午夜时分达到天空的最高点，并在日出时分在西方落下。

paras.en: You can find it in the constellation Taurus, close to the Pleiades open star cluster, also known as the Seven Sisters and M45. Uranus will be a few degrees southeast of the cluster, appearing as a faint point of light, about two-fifths of the distance between the Pleiades and Aldebaran, the brightest star in Taurus.
paras.zh: 您可以在金牛座找到它，靠近昴宿星团，也称为七姐妹星团和 M45。天王星将位于该星团东南方几度处，看起来像一个微弱的光点，大约是昴宿星团和金牛座最亮恒星毕宿五之间距离的五分之二。

paras.en: At magnitude +5.6, Uranus is technically visible to the naked eye under very dark skies. However, binoculars or a telescope will make it much easier to find.
paras.zh: 天王星的视星等为+5.6，在非常黑暗的天空中，理论上可以用肉眼看到它。不过，使用双筒望远镜或天文望远镜会更容易找到它。

paras.en: At opposition, Uranus will be 18.4 astronomical units (AU) from Earth — about 1.7 billion miles (2.7 billion kilometers) away. Through a telescope, it will appear as a tiny blue-green disk. Its color comes from methane in its atmosphere, which absorbs red wavelengths of sunlight.
paras.zh: 在冲日时，天王星将距离地球18.4个天文单位（AU），即约17亿英里（27亿公里）。通过望远镜观察，它将呈现为一个小小的蓝绿色圆盘。它的颜色来自其大气层中的甲烷，甲烷会吸收阳光的红色波长。

paras.en: Named after Ouranos, the ancient Greek god of the sky and the heavens, according to the Planetary Society , Uranus is one of the least understood planets in the solar system. A day on Uranus lasts for about 17 hours, and the planet rotates sideways, according to NASA. It takes 84 Earth years to orbit the sun.
paras.zh: 根据行星协会的说法，天王星以古希腊天空之神乌拉诺斯命名，是太阳系中最不为人所知的行星之一。 A day on Uranus lasts for about 17 hours, and the planet rotates sideways, according to NASA.绕太阳运行一周需要 84 个地球年。

paras.en: Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: Uranus also has 13 faint rings and at least 29 known moons, the most recent of which was found in 2025 by the James Webb Space Telescope. It was named Uranus XXVIII and orbits between the moons Ophelia and Bianca. Many of Uranus' moons are named after characters from the works of William Shakespeare and Alexander Pope.
paras.zh: 天王星还有 13 个微弱的光环和至少 29 个已知的卫星，其中最近的一颗是由詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜于 2025 年发现的。它被命名为天王星 XXVIII，在奥菲利亚卫星和比安卡卫星之间运行。天王星的许多卫星都是以威廉·莎士比亚和亚历山大·蒲柏作品中的人物命名的。

paras.en: The distant planet has been visited only once, by NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft on Jan. 24, 1986. However, contrary to what the probe found, scientists now think the planet emits its own internal heat. That could increase pressure on NASA to prepare a Uranus Orbiter and Probe (UOP), a mission concept the National Academy of Sciences recommended in 2022 as a high-priority planetary science mission for the next decade.
paras.zh: 这颗遥远的行星只在 1986 年 1 月 24 日被 NASA 的旅行者 2 号宇宙飞船访问过一次。然而，与探测器的发现相反，科学家现在认为这颗行星会散发出自己的内部热量。这可能会增加美国宇航局准备天王星轨道飞行器和探测器（UOP）的压力，这是美国国家科学院在 2022 年推荐的任务概念，作为未来十年的高度优先行星科学任务。

paras.en: Uranus will next come to opposition on Nov. 30, 2027.
paras.zh: 天王星下次冲分将于 2027 年 11 月 30 日发生。

paras.en: Jamie Carter is a Cardiff, U.K.-based freelance science journalist and a regular contributor to Live Science. He is the author of A Stargazing Program For Beginners and co-author of The Eclipse Effect, and leads international stargazing and eclipse-chasing tours. His work appears regularly in Space.com, Forbes, New Scientist, BBC Sky at Night, Sky & Telescope, and other major science and astronomy publications. He is also the editor of WhenIsTheNextEclipse.com.
paras.zh: 杰米·卡特 (Jamie Carter) 是英国卡迪夫的一名自由科学记者，也是《Live Science》的定期撰稿人。他是《初学者观星计划》一书的作者，也是《日食效应》一书的合著者，并领导国际观星和日食追逐之旅。他的作品经常出现在 Space.com、福布斯、新科学家、BBC 夜间天空、天空与望远镜以及其他主要科学和天文学出版物上。他还是 WhenIsTheNextEclipse.com 的编辑。

articles.title: Why Nobel physics prize winner Francis Halzen staked his career on an 'almost non-existent piece of reality'
articles.author: Ben Turner

paras.en: When Francis Halzen first proposed burying a $271 million telescope deep beneath the South Pole, he expected to be laughed off stage. Four decades later, it won him a Nobel Prize.
paras.zh: 当弗朗西斯·哈尔岑 (Francis Halzen) 首次提议将价值 2.71 亿美元的望远镜埋在南极深处时，他预计会被嘲笑下台。四十年后，这为他赢得了诺贝尔奖。

paras.en: Consisting of thousands of light sensors strung like rosary beads inside a cubic kilometer (0.2 cubic miles) of pristine ice, his detector, aptly named IceCube, is not an obvious way to study the universe. But Halzen, a theoretical physicist at the University of Madison-Wisconsin, isn't looking for something obvious.
paras.zh: 他的探测器由数千个像念珠一样串在一立方公里（0.2 立方英里）的原始冰中的光传感器组成，它被恰当地命名为 IceCube，并不是研究宇宙的明显方法。但威斯康星州麦迪逊大学的理论物理学家哈尔岑并不是在寻找明显的东西。

paras.en: His quarries are neutrinos, near-massless, chargeless, shapeshifters that are the most abundant material particles in existence. They form from nuclear processes and high-energy collisions, swarming out of our sun and whizzing from the outskirts of black holes. Yet though neutrinos stream through stars, planets, and us every second in their trillions, you still have a 75% chance of living your entire life without a single one striking an atom in your body.
paras.zh: 他的采石场是中微子，它们几乎无质量、无电荷、变形体，是现存最丰富的物质粒子。它们由核过程和高能碰撞形成，从太阳中涌出，从黑洞的边缘呼啸而出。然而，尽管中微子每秒以万亿计的速度流经恒星、行星和我们，但你仍有 75% 的机会一生中没有一个中微子撞击你体内的原子。

paras.en: On the rare occasions neutrinos do interact with atoms, they create charged particles that zip through water or ice faster than light does, casting a faint blue cone — the optical equivalent of a sonic boom.
paras.zh: 在极少数情况下，中微子确实会与原子相互作用，它们会产生带电粒子，这些粒子比光速更快地穿过水或冰，投射出微弱的蓝色锥体——光学上相当于音爆。

paras.en: Since 2011, IceCube has been retracing this blue light to study neutrinos produced by the most violent astrophysical events, probing energies far beyond those of Earth-based laboratories to find cracks in the laws of physics.
paras.zh: 自 2011 年以来，IceCube 一直在追踪这种蓝光​​，以研究最剧烈的天体物理事件产生的中微子，探测远远超出地球实验室能量的能量，以寻找物理定律的裂缝。

paras.en: In the wake of his Nobel win, Live Science sat down with Halzen to discuss neutrinos, IceCube's journey from fanciful proposal to historic success, and the future of mapping the cosmos using the trails of ghosts. Here's what he had to say.
paras.zh: 在获得诺贝尔奖后，Live Science 与 Halzen 坐下来讨论了中微子、IceCube 从奇思妙想到历史性成功的历程，以及利用幽灵轨迹绘制宇宙地图的未来。这是他不得不说的。

paras.en: Ben Turner: What first got you into physics?
paras.zh: 本·特纳：是什么首先让你进入物理学领域的？

paras.en: Francis Halzen: I got into physics kind of by accident. When I came out of high school, I didn't know what to do. I was interested in languages, I was interested in science. I'm a bad example of an inspirational career.
paras.zh: Francis Halzen：我进入物理学领域有点偶然。当我高中毕业时，我不知道该做什么。我对语言感兴趣，我对科学感兴趣。我是励志职业的一个坏例子。

paras.en: I did mathematics because in the Belgian system it was very much in the old French style — in fact, it was created by Napoleon — and hadn't changed when I was in high school. And so, if you were a good student, mathematics was the thing to do, right? So I did mathematics for two years, and then I did physics in parallel, and then switched to physics. When I switched, I got a professor who became my supervisor and he gave me the paper of George Zweig [who co-proposed quarks alongside Murray Gell-Mann] on quarks, which was a fundamental discovery.
paras.zh: 我学数学是因为在比利时的体系中，它非常具有古老的法国风格——事实上，它是由拿破仑创建的——并且在我上高中时没有改变。所以，如果你是一个好学生，数学就是你要做的事情，对吗？所以我学了两年数学，然后并行做物理，然后又转到物理。当我转行时，一位教授成为了我的导师，他给了我乔治·茨威格（George Zweig）（他与默里·盖尔曼（Murray Gell-Mann）共同提出夸克）关于夸克的论文，这是一项基本发现。

paras.en: George Zweig was actually an experimentalist, and he made these calculations using little figures. I recognized, as I had done mathematics, that this was group theory; and I said "I can do this better." I actually wrote several papers on the subject; and so suddenly I was a theoretical particle physicist. And that's what I still am. My heart never left particle physics.
paras.zh: 乔治·茨威格实际上是一位实验家，他用小数字进行了这些计算。正如我研究数学一样，我认识到这是群论。我说“我可以做得更好”。事实上我写了几篇关于这个主题的论文；突然之间，我成为了一名理论粒子物理学家。我现在仍然是这样。我的心从未离开过粒子物理学。

paras.en: BT: And then quarks eventually became neutrinos for you. Why neutrinos?
paras.zh: BT：然后夸克最终变成了中微子。为什么是中微子？

paras.en: FH: I actually didn't study neutrinos until I really got involved in starting this experiment. Half of my career, which was passed by the time I started AMANDA [IceCube's prototype] and IceCube, I really had very little overlap with neutrino physics.
paras.zh: FH：实际上，在我真正参与开始这个实验之前，我并没有研究中微子。我职业生涯的一半，到我开始 AMANDA [IceCube 的原型] 和 IceCube 时就已经过去了，我与中微子物理学确实没有什么重叠。

paras.en: I became interested in neutrinos again [while] solving a theoretical problem. In fact, the idea of detecting neutrinos with ice originated with [Gurgen] Askaryan, an Armenian physicist, in 1963.
paras.zh: 在解决一个理论问题时，我再次对中微子产生了兴趣。事实上，用冰探测中微子的想法最初是由亚美尼亚物理学家 [Gurgen] Askaryan 在 1963 年提出的。

paras.en: You cannot see neutrinos. They have no charge. They have basically no mass. So the way to detect neutrinos is when they interact with the nucleus. We are moving now in a sea of neutrinos, but neutrinos don't interact with atoms, so we don't know it. But if they accidentally hit the nucleus of an atom, then they make a nuclear reaction, and that emits charged particles. It's like a spark, and you can detect a spark with antennas.
paras.zh: 你看不到中微子。他们不收费。它们基本上没有质量。因此，检测中微子的方法是当它们与原子核相互作用时。我们现在正在中微子的海洋中移动，但中微子不与原子相互作用，所以我们不知道。但如果它们不小心撞到原子核，就会发生核反应，并发射带电粒子。它就像一个火花，你可以用天线检测到火花。

paras.en: So Askaryan's idea was to put radio antennas in ice. We are doing exactly that. But instead of looking at the radio emission, we look at the light that's emitted, which is just blue light. We use that blue light to reconstruct the neutrino and all its properties, including its direction — [that's] why it is a telescope, right?
paras.zh: 所以阿斯卡良的想法是将无线电天线放在冰里。我们正在这样做。但我们不是观察无线电发射，而是观察发出的光，它只是蓝光。我们使用蓝光来重建中微子及其所有属性，包括它的方向——[这就是]为什么它是望远镜，对吗？

paras.en: I was worrying about that experiment because they had not been able to calculate the power of the spark, so they didn't know if this worked or not. Then someone told me at some point that the Russians — I guess it was still the Soviet Union — are actually doing this at a station in Antarctica by pointing [radio] dishes into the ice. I said: "This is crazy."
paras.zh: 我很担心那个实验，因为他们无法计算火花的功率，所以他们不知道这是否有效。然后有人在某个时候告诉我，俄罗斯人——我猜仍然是苏联——实际上正在南极洲的一个站通过将[无线电]天线指向冰中来做到这一点。我说：“这太疯狂了。”

paras.en: But I had ice all over my brain, right? When I saw in the late 80s how difficult it was to do these experiments in deep ocean water it was normal to have the idea to do it in ice. And, to our credit, we understood that it actually may be simpler.
paras.zh: 但我的脑子里全是冰，对吧？当我在 80 年代末看到在深海水中进行这些实验有多么困难时，有在冰中进行这些实验的想法是很正常的。而且，值得赞扬的是，我们知道它实际上可能更简单。

paras.en: BT: Why is being able to calculate the power of the spark so important?
paras.zh: BT：为什么计算火花的功率如此重要？

paras.en: FH: [It's about] how much light is made, and how far it travels through your detector. If you don't make enough light, and it's immediately absorbed, then you have no experiment.
paras.zh: FH：[它是关于]产生了多少光，以及它通过探测器的传播距离。如果你没有发出足够的光，并且它立即被吸收，那么你就没有实验可言。

paras.en: The reason we are talking to each other [today] is because we had this incredible luck that blue light travels 100 meters [328 feet] and more through this ancient ice without being absorbed. So it's relatively easy to instrument an ice block of a kilometer cubed with light sensors.
paras.zh: 我们今天互相交谈的原因是因为我们非常幸运，蓝光可以穿过这片古老的冰层传播 100 米（328 英尺）甚至更远，而不会被吸收。因此，用光传感器检测一公里立方的冰块相对容易。

paras.en: BT: When you first proposed melting 61 two-kilometre [1.2-mile] holes in the coldest place on Earth, you said you expected to be laughed off stage. Then when you weren't, you said you continued to worry about it. What were you worrying about?
paras.zh: BT：当你第一次提议在地球上最冷的地方融化 61 个两公里 [1.2 英里] 的洞时，你说你预计会在舞台下被嘲笑。然后当你不这样做时，你说你仍然担心它。你在担心什么？

paras.en: FH: Well, the worry was that I was totally out of my league. I didn't understand glaciology, I am not an experimentalist, so I didn't really grasp the technological challenges of doing this. The experiments in water were not doing very well: There was the leading experiment off the coast of Hawaii [the Deep Underwater Muon And Neutrino Detector, or DUMAND, project] and it happened that the man leading this experiment, John Learned, was a good friend of mine, and I eventually contacted him.
paras.zh: FH：嗯，担心的是我完全超出了我的范围。我不懂冰川学，我不是实验学家，所以我并没有真正掌握这样做的技术挑战。水中实验进展得不太好：在夏威夷海岸进行了一项领先的实验（深水下介子和中微子探测器，或 DUMAND 项目），而领导这项实验的人约翰·勒尼德（John Learned）碰巧是我的好朋友，我最终联系了他。

paras.en: And the glaciology, of course. Nobody knew what the optical properties were of ice at a depth of one kilometer [0.6 miles] or more under the South Pole. There were [ice] cores that had been taken, but cores are small — the size of a teacup — so you cannot tell how far the light travels [through the ice]. So people thought it was a cute idea that would never work.
paras.zh: 当然还有冰川学。没有人知道南极以下一公里（0.6 英里）或更深处的冰的光学特性是什么。有[冰]核心已被采取，但核心很小——茶杯大小——所以你无法知道光[通过冰]传播了多远。所以人们认为这是一个永远行不通的可爱想法。

paras.en: If I had known more about glaciology, about hot water drilling, and about the technical challenges, I would never have started this experiment. It's the advantage of being ignorant. It's why young people make great discoveries, and when you're 82 years old you don't make this progress — you know too much.
paras.zh: 如果我对冰川学、热水钻探以及技术挑战有更多了解，我就永远不会开始这个实验。这就是无知的好处。这就是为什么年轻人会做出伟大的发现，而当你 82 岁的时候，你就无法取得这样的进步了——你知道的太多了。

paras.en: BT: You speak about AMANDA and IceCube with a lot of ambivalence. You said you "got dragged into it by accident" and "tried to get out of it many times."
paras.zh: BT：您在谈到 AMANDA 和 IceCube 时带着很多矛盾的情绪。你说你“不小心被卷入其中”并且“多次试图摆脱它”。

paras.en: FH: Oh yes, absolutely. You know, theorists write two types of papers: [the first are] papers where they think they contribute to the progress of science — they usually don't. But the other type of paper is just to show you're smart. And this was definitely in the second category. And then two people from Berkeley [Doug Lowder and Andrew Westphal] actually started the experiment.
paras.zh: FH：哦，是的，绝对是。你知道，理论家写两种类型的论文：[第一种是]他们认为对科学进步做出贡献的论文——但他们通常不会。但另一种类型的论文只是为了表明你很聪明。这绝对属于第二类。然后来自伯克利的两个人 [Doug Lowder 和 Andrew Westphal] 实际上开始了这个实验。

paras.en: BT: Well, you won a Nobel Prize for it. If you wanted to look smart, you succeeded.
paras.zh: BT：嗯，你因此获得了诺贝尔奖。如果你想看起来很聪明，你就成功了。

paras.en: FH: Yeah, without a lot of luck, I wouldn't be sitting here.
paras.zh: FH：是的，如果没有太多运气，我就不会坐在这里。

paras.en: BT: But surely it wasn't just showing off? Despite all of the uncertainties and worries, there must have been something about neutrinos — these barely detectable, misbehaving particles — that's so important it made you stick around. What's the draw to learn about them?
paras.zh: BT：但这肯定不只是炫耀吗？尽管存在所有的不确定性和担忧，但中微子——这些几乎无法检测到、行为不端的粒子——一定有一些东西，它是如此重要，以至于让你留下来。了解它们有什么吸引力？

paras.en: FH: Neutrinos are something really special, right? When you look at the Standard Model of matter [which describes all the known particles and forces], it has quarks, leptons, and neutrinos.
paras.zh: FH：中微子确实很特别，对吧？当你查看物质的标准模型（它描述了所有已知的粒子和力）时，它有夸克、轻子和中微子。

paras.en: But neutrinos are special in the sense that they're supposed to have no mass. They're just like photons: they travel at the speed of light, so you can do astronomy with them. But then they have the advantage that they go through planets; they go through the Earth; they reach you from the beginning of time; they reach you from the edge of the universe. They're this almost non-existent piece of reality.
paras.zh: 但中微子很特殊，因为它们应该没有质量。它们就像光子一样：它们以光速传播，所以你可以用它们进行天文学研究。但他们的优势是可以穿越行星；他们穿越地球；它们从一开始就到达你身边；他们从宇宙的边缘到达你。它们几乎是不存在的现实。

paras.en: So they always had a special fascination. We knew they existed since 1930; because without neutrinos you cannot change a proton into a neutron. They were ghosts — that's where the name "ghost particle" comes from. They were part of physics, and particle physics, and nuclear physics, but they had never been seen.
paras.zh: 所以他们总是有一种特殊的魅力。我们自 1930 年起就知道它们的存在；因为没有中微子就无法将质子变成中子。它们是幽灵——这就是“幽灵粒子”这个名字的由来。它们是物理学、粒子物理学和核物理学的一部分，但从未被发现。

paras.en: It's only in 1956 that [Frederick] Reines and [Clyde] Cowen finally discovered the neutrino by putting a detector close to a nuclear reactor, where there are lots of them. If they don't interact, then you compensate by going to a place where there are lots of them, and a nuclear reactor was an opportunity.
paras.zh: 直到 1956 年，[Frederick] Reines 和 [Clyde] Cowen 才终于在核反应堆附近放置探测器发现了中微子，因为那里有很多中微子。如果它们不相互作用，那么你可以通过去一个有很多它们的地方来补偿，而核反应堆就是一个机会。

paras.en: It's a fascinating particle. Of course now it fascinates us because they do have mass, which is not allowed by the structure of the Standard Model, and so they carry some information on new physics — the new physics we are looking for with the Large Hadron Collider in Geneva. They are the particles that have carried the message of that new physics most directly, and that's our domain.
paras.zh: 这是一个令人着迷的粒子。当然，现在它让我们着迷，因为它们确实有质量，这是标准模型的结构所不允许的，因此它们携带了一些关于新物理学的信息——我们正在日内瓦的大型强子对撞机寻找的新物理学。它们是最直接地传递新物理学信息的粒子，这就是我们的领域。

paras.en: We should have all the advantages. Sadly, they just behave like the Standard Model in everything we have done over the first 15 years of this experiment.
paras.zh: 我们应该拥有所有的优势。遗憾的是，在我们在这个实验的前 15 年中所做的一切中，它们的表现都与标准模型相同。

paras.en: BT: Famously, in 1993 to '94, microscopic air bubbles trapped in Antarctica's ice scattered neutrinos' blue light like frosted glass, nearly killing the project. You saved it by drilling to where the ice sheet's weight crushed those bubbles out of existence, up to 2.5 kilometers [1.6 miles] beneath the surface and one kilometer deeper than you originally planned. How hard was that?
paras.zh: BT：众所周知，1993 年至 94 年，困在南极洲冰层中的微小气泡像磨砂玻璃一样散射了中微子的蓝光，几乎毁掉了该项目。您通过钻探到冰盖的重量将这些气泡压碎而消失的位置来保存它，该位置位于地表以下 2.5 公里（1.6 英里）处，比您最初计划的深一公里。那有多难？

paras.en: FH: Well, the drilling almost killed the project twice.
paras.zh: FH：嗯，两次钻探几乎毁掉了这个项目。

paras.en: It's actually an interesting story, because we now detect a neutrino every minute as we are speaking, but they are produced in the atmosphere. They [atmospheric neutrinos] are our background — interesting background, but a background.
paras.zh: 这实际上是一个有趣的故事，因为我们现在在说话时每分钟都会检测到中微子，但它们是在大气中产生的。它们[大气中微子]是我们的背景——有趣的背景，但只是一个背景。

paras.en: After we had solved all these problems and could detect neutrinos, the only threshold to cross was to produce a drill that could build IceCube. That involves melting ice over two and a half kilometers over an area the size of a basketball. The technique existed in glaciers, but [produced] a shallow hole about the size of a bottle of wine.
paras.zh: 当我们解决了所有这些问题并能够探测到中微子之后，唯一要跨越的门槛就是生产出可以建造冰立方的钻头。这涉及到在篮球大小的区域内融化两公里半的冰。这项技术存在于冰川中，但[产生]了一个大约一瓶酒大小的浅洞。

paras.en: So we went to companies specialized in building hoses, and we needed a hose that was 2.5 kilometers long. The first company we went to told us: "Look, you hang a hose the size of a tea cup over two and a half kilometers of hot water and what do you think will happen?" It will collapse. Even the theorists could understand that it would collapse.
paras.zh: 于是我们去找了专门生产软管的公司，我们需要一根2.5公里长的软管。我们去的第一家公司告诉我们：“看，你把一根茶杯大小的软管挂在两公里半的热水上，你认为会发生什么？”它会崩溃。即使是理论家也能理解它会崩溃。

paras.en: And that was the end of the project. For weeks I thought it was finished. I told one of our engineers, a brilliant guy who contributed much more than what I'm going to tell you, and he didn't give up. He found a company in Padua, Italy, near Venice and they said: "We can build anything." And they did.
paras.zh: 项目就这样结束了。几个星期以来我都以为事情已经完成了。我告诉了我们的一位工程师，他是一位才华横溢的人，他的贡献比我要告诉你的要多得多，他并没有放弃。他在威尼斯附近的意大利帕多瓦找到了一家公司，他们说：“我们可以建造任何东西。”他们做到了。

paras.en: Then, when we started drilling, it was still a problem. We drilled one hole over a whole [South Pole] season. We had brilliant engineers working on this totally new piece of equipment — you have no idea how complex this is — and they learned from the mistakes of the first year and the second year it worked. They deployed 86 strings without ever failing, which is amazing actually. It's like when you launch 86 satellites, you're probably going to fail some. That's what we thought. But they never did.
paras.zh: 然后，当我们开始钻孔时，这仍然是一个问题。我们在整个[南极]季节钻了一个洞。我们有才华横溢的工程师致力于这款全新设备——你不知道这有多复杂——他们从第一年和第二年的错误中吸取了教训。他们部署了 86 个字符串，从未失败过，这实际上是令人惊奇的。这就像当你发射 86 颗卫星时，你可能会失败一些。这就是我们的想法。但他们从来没有这样做过。

paras.en: BT: The detector went online in 2011, then that year and the next came "Bert" and "Ernie" — the first ever detections of astrophysical neutrinos from beyond our solar system. After all that effort, all those near misses, and every doubt you ever had, what did it feel like when they arrived?
paras.zh: BT：该探测器于 2011 年上线，然后是那一年，接下来是“伯特”和“厄尼”——首次探测到太阳系以外的天体物理中微子。经过所有的努力、所有的惊险事件以及你曾经有过的每一个疑问，当他们到达时感觉如何？

paras.en: FH: We were not sure we believed it. It was clear then that this was a major discovery — if it was true. It took us six months or more to have the courage to write the paper.
paras.zh: FH：我们不确定我们是否相信它。很明显，如果这是真的的话，这将是一个重大发现。我们花了六个月或更长时间才有勇气写这篇论文。

paras.en: I remember seeing the first events on my screen in October of 2012, and they looked like they couldn't have come from the atmosphere — such high energy! We discovered the first two serendipitously in the first two years of data. Then, after we went to look for more knowing what these events look like, we had 28. So we had the courage to publish.
paras.zh: 我记得 2012 年 10 月在屏幕上看到第一个事件，它们看起来不可能来自大气层——能量如此之高！我们在前两年的数据中偶然发现了前两个。然后，当我们去寻找更多了解这些事件是什么样子的信息后，我们得到了 28 个。所以我们有勇气发布。

paras.en: But then, three weeks later, we were declared the physics breakthrough of the year. I must say I was not happy about that. I had to give a press conference, and I was all the time thinking: "If this is not true, how am I going to walk this back?"
paras.zh: 但三周后，我们被宣布为年度物理学突破。我必须说我对此并不满意。我不得不召开新闻发布会，我一直在想：“如果这不是真的，我该如何挽回呢？”

paras.en: It took me quite a while to convince myself that this wasn't just something that looked like cosmic neutrinos. But this is such an unusual corner of science, you don't know whether you are fooled by some other phenomena you haven't thought of.
paras.zh: 我花了很长时间才说服自己这不仅仅是看起来像宇宙中微子的东西。但这是科学的一个不寻常的角落，你不知道你是否被其他一些你没有想到的现象所愚弄。

paras.en: FH: Well now we are seeing sources of neutrinos. You see 100 neutrinos come from an active galaxy, and you point [a different telescope] back at it with 0.04 degree resolution. There's no doubt now. But being convinced was a continuous process; at least in my case. My colleagues always refer to me as a total optimist, but it took me some time. I was not my usual self on this.
paras.zh: FH：现在我们看到了中微子的来源。您看到 100 个中微子来自一个活跃的星系，然后您将 [另一台望远镜] 以 0.04 度的分辨率指向它。现在毫无疑问了。但被说服是一个持续的过程；至少就我而言。我的同事总是称我为一个彻底的乐观主义者，但这花了我一些时间。在这件事上我和平时不一样了。

paras.en: But now there's no doubt. The statistics of observing cosmic neutrinos is totally impossible [to deny] with the precision we have now. But we're talking about 14 years of data. It's really incredible how quickly we've progressed.
paras.zh: 但现在毫无疑问了。以我们现在的精度，观测宇宙中微子的统计数据是完全不可能[否认]的。但我们谈论的是 14 年的数据。我们进步的速度真是令人难以置信。

paras.en: And you realize that, officially, none of the things we see have been confirmed by someone else. There are two experiments, [Baikal-G in Lake Baikal and [KM3NeT] in the Mediterranean Sea, but they're under construction. And they both have produced some kind of evidence, but a real confirmation of seeing the same thing we see has still not happened. So the Nobel Prize [Committee] had more courage than me.
paras.zh: 你意识到，从官方角度来看，我们所看到的一切都没有得到其他人的证实。有两个实验，贝加尔湖的[Baikal-G]和地中海的[KM3NeT]，但它们正在建设中。他们都提供了某种证据，但真正证实我们看到的东西仍然没有发生。所以诺奖[组委会]比我更有勇气。

paras.en: BT: You were in a hotel room in Italy when the call came from Stockholm. What went through your mind in the first quiet moments after hanging up?
paras.zh: BT：当斯德哥尔摩打来电话时，你正在意大利的一家酒店房间里。挂断电话后最初安静的时刻你脑子里在想什么？

paras.en: FH: Well, after hanging up, I was sent a Zoom link, and they asked me questions, which I answered. But I didn't know that I was actually giving a press conference. I still haven't looked back at that press conference.
paras.zh: FH：嗯，挂断电话后，我收到了一个 Zoom 链接，他们问了我问题，我回答了。但我不知道我实际上是在召开新闻发布会。我仍然没有回头看那次新闻发布会。

paras.en: But that's how crazy it was, because I had forgotten that it was Nobel season. The call came by total surprise. Well, it wasn't a total surprise because there's a game of predicting the Nobel Prizes. And I had been there [in the running to win] for several years.
paras.zh: 但这就是多么疯狂，因为我忘记了那是诺贝尔奖季节。这个电话来得完全出乎意料。嗯，这并不完全令人惊讶，因为有一个预测诺贝尔奖的游戏。我已经在那里[为了获胜]好几年了。

paras.en: So I cannot say that I was unaware of this. But this was a difficult season for me, right? People literally would send me condolence messages every year for not winning. And they meant it — they're my friends — but it makes you feel strange. You feel you've disappointed your collaborators.
paras.zh: 所以我不能说我不知道​​这一点。但这对我来说是一个艰难的赛季，对吧？每年人们都会因为我没有获奖而给我发来哀悼信息。他们是认真的——他们是我的朋友——但这让你感觉很奇怪。你觉得你让你的合作者失望了。

paras.en: So that's the first thing I thought: "Okay, the problem is solved now. Everybody can get credit for this experiment." And deservedly. Because IceCube was becoming mostly me, and data and science. The fact of its history and the contributions people made was being forgotten very fast. The great thing about this Nobel Prize is that it's for a difficult problem that was solved by so many brilliant people over almost four decades.
paras.zh: 这就是我想到的第一件事：“好吧，现在问题解决了。每个人都可以因为这个实验而获得荣誉。”并且当之无愧。因为 IceCube 正在成为我、数据和科学的主要部分。它的历史事实和人们做出的贡献很快就被遗忘了。这个诺贝尔奖的伟大之处在于它是为了一个难题，而这个难题是由许多杰出人士在近四十年中解决的。

paras.en: BT: Aside from winning the Nobel, what's been the highlight of working on IceCube?
paras.zh: BT：除了获得诺贝尔奖之外，IceCube 工作的亮点是什么？

paras.en: FH: The highlight for me was to show that the technique works. Seeing these neutrinos go through the Earth, and then through the detector, was incredibly exciting because there was no doubt you were looking at a stream of particles going through your detector initiated by neutrinos that came through the Earth. There was no doubt. What you see is what you get.
paras.zh: FH：对我来说最重要的是证明这项技术是有效的。看到这些中微子穿过地球，然后穿过探测器，是非常令人兴奋的，因为毫无疑问，你看到的是由穿过地球的中微子引发的穿过探测器的粒子流。毫无疑问。所见即所得。

paras.en: We had this attitude that if you build something this big you're going to do interesting science. This is so different from anything that has been built before. I don't want to insult astronomers, but our joke was: "We are all particle physicists, guys. God forbid we have to do astronomy." But that's what we are doing.
paras.zh: 我们的态度是，如果你建造了这么大的东西，你就会做有趣的科学。这与以前建造的任何东西都非常不同。我不想侮辱天文学家，但我们的笑话是：“伙计们，我们都是粒子物理学家。上帝不允许我们从事天文学研究。”但这就是我们正在做的事情。

paras.en: I must say, it's very, very exciting to learn astronomy when you're 82 years old.
paras.zh: 我必须说，当你82岁时学习天文学是非常非常令人兴奋的。

paras.en: BT: IceCube–Gen2 is targeted to come online by 2033 and will be eight times larger than the original detector. What do you want for its future?
paras.zh: BT：IceCube–Gen2 的目标是在 2033 年上线，并将比原始探测器大八倍。你对它的未来有何期望？

paras.en: FH: Whenever I give a talk, I have a list of conclusions, and my first is always that neutrino astronomy exists, and that's our contribution. Doing neutrino astronomy will require more instruments, bigger instruments. In astronomy there's not just one telescope, right? To do real astronomy we'll need more instruments covering the sky completely, and we'll need more neutrinos with better angular resolution.
paras.zh: FH：每当我发表演讲时，我都会列出一系列结论，而我的第一个结论始终是中微子天文学的存在，这就是我们的贡献。进行中微子天文学需要更多、更大的仪器。天文学中不只有一台望远镜，对吧？为了进行真正的天文学研究，我们需要更多完全覆盖天空的仪器，并且需要更多具有更好角分辨率的中微子。

paras.en: The nice thing is that will happen: There are ambitious projects in China now, and [the upgrade of] our own project too. How can you pass it up? Because now the technology is much better: we understand the ice perfectly; we can design this detector, optimize it, and gain an order of magnitude [improvement] for the same cost as the original.
paras.zh: 令人高兴的是，这将会发生：中国现在有雄心勃勃的项目，还有我们自己的项目[升级]。你怎么能错过呢？因为现在的技术好多了：我们完全了解冰；我们可以设计这个探测器，对其进行优化，并以与原始探测器相同的成本获得一个数量级的[改进]。

paras.en: BT: You famously don't like to make predictions, even one year ahead, about what we might learn about neutrinos. So I'm going to try to be sly with this final question: What do you hope the future has in store for neutrino astronomy?
paras.zh: BT：众所周知，您不喜欢对我们可能了解的中微子知识做出预测，即使是一年后也是如此。因此，我将尝试狡猾地回答最后一个问题：您希望中微子天文学的未来如何？

paras.en: FH: I hope for a galactic supernova [within the Milky Way]. I don't know if you know the history, but in 1987 there was a supernova in a [nearby] satellite galaxy, but it [meant physicists] detected 20 neutrinos. And what we learned from these neutrinos is incredible — literally thousands of papers have been written about those 20 neutrinos, and they're all interesting.
paras.zh: FH：我希望[银河系内]出现银河超新星。我不知道你是否了解历史，但是在1987年，[附近的]卫星星系中出现了一颗超新星，但它[意味着物理学家]检测到了20个中微子。我们从这些中微子中学到的东西令人难以置信——实际上已经有数千篇关于这 20 个中微子的论文，而且它们都很有趣。

paras.en: Neutrinos are supposed to have no mass and be just like photons. The best limit we could set on the [tiny and still unexplained] mass of the neutrino came from that supernova. So we made very fundamental measurements that we hadn't been able to make with [laboratory] neutrino beams. And then the whole story that a star really collapses into a neutron star. All that suddenly became reality. I was not, and am still not, an astronomer, but from the point of view of stellar physics this was a major event.
paras.zh: 中微子应该没有质量，就像光子一样。我们可以对中微子的[微小且仍无法解释的]质量设定的最佳限制来自于超新星。因此，我们进行了非常基本的测量，这是我们无法使用[实验室]中微子束进行的。然后是恒星真的塌缩成中子星的整个故事。这一切突然变成了现实。我过去不是，现在仍然不是天文学家，但从恒星物理学的角度来看，这是一件重大事件。

paras.en: - What if space and time don't exist? Physicists are chasing hints that our reality emerges from something deeper
paras.zh: - 如果空间和时间不存在怎么办？物理学家正在寻找我们的现实源于更深层次的暗示

paras.en: - 'A real revolution': The James Webb telescope is upending our understanding of the biggest, oldest black holes in the universe
paras.zh: - “一场真正的革命”：詹姆斯·韦伯望远镜正在颠覆我们对宇宙中最大、最古老黑洞的理解

paras.en: - 'It's more than a hope, it's a guarantee': The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's 10-year movie of the universe is about to 'blow our minds,' chief scientist Tony Tyson says
paras.zh: - “这不仅仅是希望，更是保证”：首席科学家托尼·泰森表示，维拉·C·鲁宾天文台的 10 年宇宙电影即将“让我们大吃一惊”

paras.en: Now, instead of three experiments, we have multiple neutrino detectors of all kinds. Some will detect thousands of neutrinos; we'll detect a million neutrinos. We can't actually reconstruct them, but we can make a very detailed movie telling you everything that went on in a supernova while the star collapsed and then exploded. The science we will do from a few seconds of data will be incredible.
paras.zh: 现在，我们不再是三个实验，而是拥有多个各种中微子探测器。有些将探测到数千个中微子；有些则将探测到中微子。我们将探测到一百万个中微子。我们实际上无法重建它们，但我们可以制作一部非常详细的电影，告诉您超新星坍缩然后爆炸时发生的一切。我们将通过几秒钟的数据进行科学研究，这将是令人难以置信的。

paras.en: I can tell you it hasn't happened since the mid-1990s because we have been looking for it continuously with AMANDA and Ice-Cube. There are supposed to be like two per century. We are due.
paras.zh: 我可以告诉你，自 20 世纪 90 年代中期以来，这种情况就没有发生过，因为我们一直在与 AMANDA 和 Ice-Cube 一起寻找它。每个世纪应该有大约两个。我们到期了。

paras.en: Editor's note: This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.
paras.zh: 编者注：为了清晰起见，本次采访经过编辑和精简。

paras.en: Ben Turner is the features editor at Live Science. He covers physics and astronomy, among other topics such as tech and climate change. He graduated from University College London with a degree in particle physics before training as a journalist. When he's not writing, Ben enjoys reading literature, playing the guitar and losing at chess.
paras.zh: Ben Turner 是 Live Science 的专题编辑。他涵盖物理学和天文学，以及技术和气候变化等其他主题。他毕业于伦敦大学学院，获得粒子物理学学位，之后接受记者培训。当他不写作时，本喜欢阅读文学作品、弹吉他和下国际象棋。

articles.title: Medieval chain mail discovered during underwater excavation of 15th-century 'floating castle' that sank off Sweden
articles.author: Kristina Killgrove

paras.en: Archaeologists have recovered high-quality chain mail armor from the 15th-century wreck of Gribshunden or Griffin, a royal warship that doubled as a "floating castle" for King Hans of Denmark. The ship exploded and sank in 1495, but maritime archaeologists have just begun exploring the area beneath the forecastle, an elevated combat platform at the front of the ship, where they discovered the armor and a unique munitions chest.
paras.zh: 考古学家从15世纪沉船“格里布松登号”（又名“狮鹫号”）的残骸中出土了高品质的锁子甲。这艘皇家战舰曾是丹麦国王汉斯的“海上城堡”。这艘船于1495年爆炸沉没，但海洋考古学家刚刚开始探索船首楼（位于船首的凸起式战斗平台）下方的区域，在那里发现了这件铠甲和一个独特的弹药箱。

paras.en: The chain mail was, "rather surprisingly, completely exposed," Rolf Warming, an archaeologist at Stockholm University and lead investigator of the Griffin project in collaboration with Södertörn University, told Live Science in an email. "It was only by chance that we came across it, and it shows just how much is still on the wreck site."
paras.zh: 斯德哥尔摩大学考古学家、与南顿大学合作的格里芬项目首席研究员罗尔夫·沃明在一封电子邮件中告诉《生活科学》，“令人惊讶的是，这封连锁邮件完全暴露了”。 “我们只是偶然发现了它，它表明了残骸现场还有多少东西。”

paras.en: The mail armor was made of copper alloy and was found in a part of the ship that may have been used as a storage area for military gear, according to a Nov. 24 statement. "Historical sources indicate that German mercenaries, or Landsknechts, were aboard Griffin when it sank in 1495," Rodrigo Pacheco-Ruiz, an archaeologist at the University of Southampton in the U.K. who is the co-investigator on the project, said in the statement. The mercenaries may have stored their armor in the area, "although we've yet to establish a precise function for the space," Pacheco-Ruiz said.
paras.zh: 根据 11 月 24 日的一份声明，邮件装甲由铜合金制成，是在船的一部分发现的，该部分可能被用作军用装备的存储区域。该项目的联合调查员、英国南安普顿大学考古学家罗德里戈·帕切科·鲁伊斯在声明中表示：“历史资料显示，1495 年格里芬号沉没时，德国雇佣兵（或称 Landsknechts）就在船上。”帕切科-鲁伊斯说，雇佣兵可能已经在该地区存放了他们的装甲，“尽管我们尚未确定该空间的精确功能”。

paras.en: The 15th-century warship was rediscovered in the Baltic Sea off the south coast of Sweden in the 1970s but formally identified by archaeologists as Griffin in 2013.
paras.zh: 这艘 15 世纪的军舰于 20 世纪 70 年代在瑞典南海岸附近的波罗的海被重新发现，但考古学家于 2013 年正式确认为格里芬号。

paras.en: Griffin was the flagship of the naval fleet of King Hans of Denmark and Norway. In 1495, Hans was sailing to Kalmar in Sweden to negotiate a political alliance and force Sweden back into a union with Denmark and Norway. He had brought with him around 150 German mercenary soldiers. "It was important to demonstrate military prowess, and the German and Swiss mercenaries were the finest you could get at that time," Warming told Live Science.
paras.zh: 格里芬号是丹麦和挪威国王汉斯海军舰队的旗舰。 1495 年，汉斯航行到瑞典卡尔马，谈判政治联盟并迫使瑞典重新与丹麦和挪威结盟。他带来了大约150名德国雇佣兵。沃明告诉《生活科学》杂志：“展示军事实力非常重要，德国和瑞士的雇佣兵是当时最优秀的。”

paras.en: During a stop at the port of Ronneby in what is now Sweden, Griffin caught fire, perhaps after being struck by lightning, and sank. Eyewitnesses who escaped reported that many men died in the tragic event. King Hans, however, was onshore when the warship sank.
paras.zh: 在停泊在现在瑞典的龙讷比港期间，格里芬号可能是被闪电击中后起火，然后沉没。逃脱的目击者报告说，许多人在这场悲惨事件中死亡。然而，当军舰沉没时，汉斯国王正在岸上。

paras.en: The warship has been well-preserved over the centuries thanks to the low salinity of the Baltic waters and the lack of shipworms, marine mollusks also known as the "termites of the sea" because of the damage they do to wood.
paras.zh: 由于波罗的海水域盐度低且缺乏船蛆，海洋软体动物也被称为“海中白蚁”，因为它们对木材造成损害，这艘军舰几个世纪以来一直保存完好。

paras.en: Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: The chain mail recovered in October is of exceptionally high quality, Warming said in the statement, but it was not necessarily the armor of an elite knight. "This kind of armour could remain in use for extended periods, often undergoing repairs or being reused, so these fragments may represent older military equipment that was still active," he said.
paras.zh: 沃明在声明中表示，10月份回收的锁子甲质量非常高，但它不一定是精英骑士的盔甲。他说：“这种装甲可以长期使用，经常进行修理或重复使用，因此这些碎片可能代表仍然活跃的旧军事装备。”

paras.en: But the researchers discovered more than just the chain mail.
paras.zh: 但研究人员发现的不仅仅是连锁邮件。

paras.en: "This year's campaign was an unusually exciting investigation!" Warming told Live Science. The team found a unique munitions chest called a "zeuglade" in German. "We have taken different samples to try to determine the contents of the chest and perhaps find traces of gunpowder," Warming said. The chest may have belonged to the German mercenaries who were aboard.
paras.zh: “今年的活动是一次异常令人兴奋的调查！”变暖告诉《生活科学》。该小组发现了一个独特的弹药箱，德语称为“zeuglade”。沃明说：“我们采集了不同的样本，试图确定箱子里的东西，或许还能找到火药的痕迹。”这个箱子可能属于船上的德国雇佣兵。

paras.en: "It was in the process of documenting the chest that I unexpectedly discovered exposed mail-armour fragments in the vicinity of the chest, along other items that could indicate more chests," Warming added. "This leads us to believe this may have been a stowage area, located just beneath the forecastle."
paras.zh: “在记录箱子的过程中，我意外地在箱子附近发现了暴露的锁甲碎片，以及其他可能表明还有更多箱子的物品，”沃明补充道。 “这让我们相信这可能是一个储藏区，位于艏楼下方。”

paras.en: Warming said that the research team is currently using chemical analysis to investigate the origins of the armor and the chest to learn more about medieval military matters.
paras.zh: 沃明表示，研究小组目前正在利用化学分析来调查盔甲和箱子的起​​源，以了解更多有关中世纪军事的信息。

paras.en: "It is probable that the mail armour belongs to the mercenaries, but it could also belong to someone else," Warming said. "The chest might also belong to them, but we don't know yet. It is actually a really fascinating research question of ours that could illuminate supply chains and the military logistics. Did the mercenary forces bring their own ammunition and tool kit aboard, or was this supplied by the royal fleet?"
paras.zh: “锁子甲很可能属于雇佣兵，但也可能属于其他人。”沃明说道。 “箱子也可能属于他们，但我们还不知道。这实际上是我们的一个非常有趣的研究问题，可以阐明供应链和军事后勤。雇佣军是否携带了自己的弹药和工具包，还是由皇家舰队提供的？”

paras.en: Kristina Killgrove is a staff writer at Live Science with a focus on archaeology and paleoanthropology news. Her articles have also appeared in venues such as Forbes, Smithsonian, and Mental Floss. Kristina holds a Ph.D. in biological anthropology and an M.A. in classical archaeology from the University of North Carolina, as well as a B.A. in Latin from the University of Virginia, and she was formerly a university professor and researcher. She has received awards from the Society for American Archaeology and the American Anthropological Association for her science writing.
paras.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·基尔格罗夫 (Kristina Killgrove) 是《Live Science》的特约撰稿人，专注于考古学和古人类学新闻。她的文章还发表在《福布斯》、《史密森尼》和《Mental Floss》等杂志上。克里斯蒂娜拥有博士学位。北卡罗来纳大学生物人类学学士学位和古典考古学硕士学位，以及北卡罗来纳大学古典考古学学士学位。她拥有弗吉尼亚大学拉丁语学位，曾任大学教授和研究员。她因其科学写作而获得美国考古学会和美国人类学协会颁发的奖项。
